As a hands-on mechanical engineer, you'll work oneverything from equipment design to production support. RequirementsProfessional Experience: 5-8 years of mechanical engineeringexperience in production or manufacturing environment, preferably withexposure to food processing, manufacturing equipment, or automatedsystems. Educational Background: Bachelor's degree in MechanicalEngineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, orrelated technical field. Strong foundation in equipment maintenance,reliability engineering, and manufacturing processes. Knowledge offood industry applications preferred. Technical Skills: Knowledge ofmanufacturing processes and production optimization techniques,familiarity with lean manufacturing principles. Strong troubleshootingabilities with hands-on experience developing mechanical solutions anddiagnosing and repairing mechanical equipment failures. Proficiencywith CAD software, process modeling tools, and manufacturing softwaresystems. Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and problem-solvingabilities with experience in root cause analysis and processtroubleshooting. Ability to interpret production data and developlonglasting cost effective engineering solutions. Operational Agility:A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset with the ability to adaptquickly in a fast-paced, dynamic startup environment. LanguageProficiency: Fluency in English and/or German, with professional levelin the later, with excellent written and verbal communication skills.Why us? jobs.occupation: Forward Deployed Engineer: Ai Solution Architect (f/m/d) (Informatiker/in)
jobs.description: As a Senior AI Solution Architect in our Forward Deployed Engineering team, you see the whole board before a single line of code is written. You partner directly with business leaders across Siemens to map complex challenges to existing data, design cross-platform architectures spanning cloud and enterprise systems, and make critical build-versus-buy decisions in days rather than quarters. You bridge deep technical AI expertise with systems thinking, acting as a force multiplier that enables agile engineering teams to deliver high-impact solutions reliably and repeatedly.What we offer you:- An attractive remuneration package- Access to Siemens share plans- 30 days of paid vacation and a variety of flexible work schedules that allow time off for you and your family- Flexible training opportunities for both your professional and personal development that you can tailor to your interestsSince each of over 300,000 team members feels that other benefits are particularly important, and we cannot list our entire benefit portfolio here, you can find more information here (https://www.siemens.com/de/en/company/jobs/benefits-what-we-offer.html) .The individual benefits are subject to regulatory, contractual, or corporate conditions.You’ll make an impact by:- Driving rapid solution architecture as the first technical expert in every engagement, translating complex business problems into viable technical blueprints within days. - Designing interconnected solutions across the entire enterprise landscape, leveraging SDC for workloads while integrating seamlessly with SAP, Salesforce, and cloud-native services. - Owning crucial architecture decisions regarding cost, latency, scalability, and stack selection, while documenting clear justifications for every trade-off. - Evaluating emerging AI technologies with rigorous skepticism, providing evidence-backed adoption recommendations and having the courage to say "not ready yet." - Staying actively involved in the codebase through technical spikes, prototype development, and pull-request reviews to ensure your architectures remain grounded in reality. - Designing from day one for seamless handover, establishing explicit interface contracts, evaluation harnesses, and operational runbooks so domain teams can run systems autonomously.Your defining qualities:- Education: You hold a university degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, AI/ML, or a comparable quantitative field, where a proven track record of shipped systems outweighs advanced degrees. - Experience & Skills:- You bring 8 or more years of experience in software architecture, AI/ML systems design, or solution architecture, including at least 3 years focused on complex enterprise AI solutions. - You demonstrate a robust history of customer-facing delivery and technical leadership, especially when navigating demanding or high-pressure stakeholder environments. - You posses hands-on coding capabilities in Python alongside TypeScript or JavaScript, allowing you to write production-grade code and build functional prototypes. - You provide expertise in cross-platform system design by successfully integrating disparate enterprise environments like SAP, Salesforce, and modern cloud services. - You exhibit deep knowledge of the modern AI stack, covering LLM failure modes, RAG architectures, evaluation metrics, vector stores, and prominent agent frameworks. - You bring working knowledge of at least one major cloud provider (Azure, AWS, or GCP) sufficient to design scalable multi-platform workloads.- Ways of working:- You demonstrate the critical ability to evaluate emerging technologies objectively, separate genuine value from hype, and communicate technical realities clearly. - You display exceptional live communication skills to sketch defensible architectures in real-time meetings and explain them fluently in business terms.- Languages: You have fluent English language skills, complemented by strong German proficiency as an advantageous asset for local stakeholder engagements.You are much more than your qualifications, and we believe in the potential of every single candidate. We look forward to getting to know you!At Siemens, we believe that feeling valued and included is the foundation for doing great work. That’s why we aim to create an inclusive workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging, and where individual perspectives and experiences are celebrated. Our commitment to fairness and respect extends to every applicant.As an equal opportunity employer (http://www.siemens.com/global/en/company/sustainability/social-commitments/belonging.html) , we welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds and particularly encourage applications from persons with disabilities.About usWe know that our business thrives only when our people thrive and unlock their full potential. That’s why you are always our top priority. Our global, diverse team is ready to support, challenge, and inspire you, helping you grow in countless ways. Together, we’ll embark on an exciting journey of discovery. Who knows where this path will lead? Join us and take an active role in shaping your future!www.siemens.de/careers (http://www.siemens.com/de/en/company/jobs.html) – if you would like to find out more about jobs & careers at Siemens.FAQ (https://www.siemens.com/en-us/company/jobs/faq/) – if you need further information on the application process.

jobs.occupation: PhD position (m/f/d) on immune reset through CAR T in chronic inflammatory diseases (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: State-of-the-art medicine and nursing care you can rely on! - Since being founded in 1815, Universitätsklinikum Erlangen has offered medicine of the highest standard and incorporated the latest insights from medical research and state-of-the-art equipment into diagnosis and therapy. More than 10.000 employees from approximately 50 different occupations are needed to provide the wide range of services offered by Universitätsklinikum Erlangen, ensuring our patients receive the very best care around the clock.As a PhD student, you will investigate how human immune-cell networks shape tissue inflammation, regeneration and response to cellular therapies. The project will focus primarily on the human immune system and combine patient-derived material with experimental models to address mechanistic questions in cellular immunology.Your tasks:- Characterizing human immune-cell populations and their functional states using multiparameter flow cytometry and high-dimensional immune phenotyping.- Investigating cellular interactions and immune networks by integrating phenotypic, functional and molecular data from immune cells and tissues.- Studying immune responses to cellular therapies, including the mechanisms underlying immune depletion, reconstitution and tissue regeneration following CD19 CAR-T-cell therapy.- Generating and analyzing molecular data using approaches such as bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing and other transcriptomic or spatial technologies.- Establishing and applying experimental models to investigate mechanisms identified in human samples, including selected mouse models of intestinal inflammation, immune reconstitution and tissue regeneration after CD19 CAR-T-cell therapy.- Developing and combining experimental and analytical approaches ranging from established methods such as ELISA, Western blotting and flow cytometry to advanced multidimensional cytometry, UMAP-based analysis and transcriptomic approaches.- The project offers substantial scope to develop an individual scientific profile. Previous experience with these techniques is welcome, but curiosity, scientific independence, willingness to learn, and enthusiasm for understanding how immune cells interact in human disease are similarly important.Essential experience/ qualifications:- Above the average motivation and work ethics- Strong theoretical and practical background in standard methods of molecular and cellular biology as well as cellular immunology- English writing and speaking skills- Ability to work together in a multi-national team that is supportive of one another- A master degree (M.Sc.) in immunology, biology, molecular biology, molecular medicine or equivalentadditional advantages:- Experience in omics data science- Hands-on experience in human immunologyWe offer:- The position is full-time and will be payed according to salary group TVL-E 13, 65% (DFG-typical rate)- Intended pay grade depending on qualifications and personal requierements- Initially, the position is limited for one year, with the possibility of an extension till the degreee is achieved- The head of the department guaranties in writing that there is funding till the degree is achieved.- Hiring process opened and will be completed asap.- An enthusiastic, interdisciplinary team of scientists and doctors- High end translational research- State-of-the-art laboratories- Two-Stepp mentoring with a hands-on mentor (post-doc) plus the PI as supervisor with high frequent project discussions for efficient development- Structured program for hard- and soft-skills in research (paper and grant writing classes, paper clubs, soft-skill training)- Notes for applicants (f/m/d) ( https://www.karriere.uk-erlangen.de/bewerbung/hinweise-fuer-bewerbende/ )- Comprehensive health promotion offers- All benefits of the public service incl. supplementary pension plan of the Versorgungsanstalt des Bundes und der Länder (VBL) (Federal and State Government Employees' Retierment Fund)- Family-friendly enviromentFurther information:Prof. Dr. med. habil. jobs.occupation: Head of Global Commodity Engineering Mechatronics 2 (f/m/d) (Betriebswirt/in (Hochschule))
jobs.description: Job Posting: Head of Global Commodity Engineering Mechatronics 2 (m/f/d)Transform the everyday.This role is responsible for leading the global strategy, governance, and execution of Material Lifecycle Management for mechanical and mechatronic components across the entire supply chain. The individual ensures suppliers, manufacturing processes, quality standards, and material strategies are optimized for cost, quality, productivity, resilience, and sustainability while driving cross-functional collaboration between Procurement, Engineering, Manufacturing, Logistics, and Quality teams worldwide.In short, this is a senior global leadership position focused on improving supplier performance, product quality, operational efficiency, and supply chain effectiveness throughout the lifecycle of mechanical and mechatronic materials and components.What we offer you- Flexible training opportunities for both your professional and personal development that you can tailor to your interests- (Global) development programs that can be customized according to your wishes and ambitions- Diverse health and wellness offerings- A work environment where you can contribute with your whole personality and truly feel like part of SiemensSince each of over 300,000 team members feels that other benefits are particularly important, and we cannot list our entire benefit portfolio here, you can find more information here.The individual benefits are subject to regulatory, contractual, or corporate conditions.How you will make an Impact with us- You will be responsible for the global strategic direction of Material Lifecycle Management for mechanical and mechatronic components, including drawing-controlled parts, assemblies, manufacturing scopes, and supply chain investments.- You will lead a team  (either directly or through collaboration models) and provide functional governance for local Material Lifecycle Management teams focused on mechatronics. You will ensure clear roles, standards, decision-making processes, and effective cross-site collaboration.- You will develop and implement a global strategy for mechatronic parts, processes, and suppliers, focusing on standardization, technical feasibility, quality capability, supply chain resilience, sustainability, Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), and productivity.- You will define supplier quality-related processes, methods, and standards for mechanical components and drive their global deployment, application, and continuous optimization across an international network.- You will oversee preventive quality planning and industrialization readiness, particularly risk assessments, Process FMEA, Control Plans, Production Control Plans, First Article Inspection/PPAP, process audits, and release procedures for drawing-controlled purchased parts.- You will establish a robust supplier problem management system with clear 8D governance, root cause analysis, effectiveness jobs.description: Wir suchen ab sofort unbefristet eineLehrkraft für Englischin TeilzeitDer derzeitige Einsatzort ist das Learning Centre in der Haidebachstraße 1 in 63808 Haibach. Mit Helen Doron bietet unser Learning Centre Kurse für Babys, Kinder und Teens in Englisch und Spanisch an, die seit 40 Jahren weltweit auf Platz Nr. 1 stehen. In unserem Learning Centre unterrichten wir derzeit 150 Kinder aller Altersgruppen, von 3 Monate bis 19 Jahre. Die Einrichtung ist räumlich ansprechend und modern ausgestattet. Wir verstehen es als unsere Aufgabe, die Familien zu unterstützen, die ihre Kinder mehrsprachig erziehen möchten, und bieten diesen Kindern eine erweiterte Sprachheimat, in der sie Englisch oder/und Spanisch mit Freude, Spiel, Spaß und ganz ohne Leistungsdruck lernen. Mit neuen Methoden werden unsere Unterrichtsinhalte von speziell ausgebildeten Lehrern altersgerecht aufbereitet und umgesetzt. Und das mit großem Erfolg!Ihre Aufgaben bei uns:- Als Helen Doron Englischlehrer unterrichten Sie bei uns zunächst 2-5 Stunden pro Woche, je nach Ihrer Flexibilität und Erfahrung im Klassenzimmer. Die Anzahl der Stunden kann sich nach 6 Monaten je Erfahrung und nach Bedarf erhöhen.-  In Abhängigkeit von Ihrer Qualifizierung unterrichten Sie eine breite Palette von spezialisierten Englischkursen für verschiedenste Altersgruppen (zwischen 3 Monaten und 19 Jahren) - In der Regel unterrichten Sie jede Ihrer Gruppen einmal pro Woche. Jede Unterrichtsstunde dauert zwischen 45, 60 und 90 Minuten. - Mit der einzigartigen Methodik von Helen Doron und dem von uns zur Verfügung gestellten Lehrmaterial werden Sie Ihre Gruppen durch Musik, mit viel Bewegung, Spiel und Spaß aktiv in Englisch unterrichten. - Um Helen Doron Teen English für Teenager zu unterrichten, werden Sie verschiedene Grammatik- und Schreibfertigkeiten auf kreative und unterhaltsame Weise vermitteln und gleichzeitig den Schülern helfen, gute Schulnoten zu erzielen. Wir freuen uns auf Sie, wenn Sie- Muttersprachler sind oder über das muttersprachliche Level C2 in Englisch in Wort und Schrift verfügen.- über das sprachliche Level B1+ in Deutsch verfügen, um mit unseren deutschsprachigen Eltern vor und nach dem Unterricht zu kommunizieren und die Fortschritte der Schüler zu besprechen. - idealerweise ein Helen Doron Diplom, einen Universitätsabschluss oder/und eine der folgenden Qualifikationen zum Unterrichten in der englischen Sprache besitzen: z.B. Celta, TEFL, PGCE, erstes/zweites Staatsexamen. Quereinsteiger sind aber auch herzlich willkommen. Wir bieten umfangreiche Schulungen und Unterstützung an.- Spaß daran haben, mit Kindern in einer aktiven, animierenden ausschließlich englischsprachigen Umgebung zu arbeiten.- eine positive Einstellung zu Kindern und zum Lernen haben.- über organisatorische Fähigkeiten verfügen.- im Landkreis Aschaffenburg wohnen.- unter der Woche nachmittags und vor allem samstags arbeiten möchten.- flexibel, verantwortungsbewusst und in hohem Maße selbstständig arbeiten können.- fit im Umgang mit Computern (v.a. iMac, iPad), Lernapps und analogen und digitalen Unterrichtsmaterialen sind.Wir bieten Ihnen:- einen angenehmen und flexiblen Beruf.- ein interessantes und vielseitiges Arbeitsfeld.- eine Lehrerausbildung, die Sie mit dem internationalen Diplom als Helen Doron Englischlehrer qualifiziert. - umfassende Möglichkeiten zur Fort- und Weiterbildung.- moderne Lehrmethoden, die Ihnen helfen, Kindern einen besseren Start ins Leben zu ermöglichen und ihnen dabei viel Freude und Spaß zu bereiten. - ein sicheres Einkommen, abhängig von Ihrer Ausbildung und Erfahrung.Einkommen für Einsteiger (pro Stunde incl. Vorbereitungszeit):- 15 EUR - ohne Universitätsabschluss, ohne pädagogischer Ausbildung - 20 EUR - mit Universitätsabschluss- 20 EUR - mit pädagogischer Ausbildung und einer mindestens zweijährigen Berufserfahrung im pädagogischen Bereich z.B. als Erzieher- 25 EUR - mit Universitätsabschluss und pädagogischer Ausbildung (z.B. Celta, TEFL, PGCE, erstes/zweites Staatsexamen) und einer mindestens zweijährigen Berufserfahrung als Lehrer- 25 EUR - mit Helen Doron Diplom und einer mindestens zweijährigen Berufserfahrung als Helen Doron LehrerSie möchten uns kennenlernen? Jetzt schnell bewerben!Ihre schriftliche Bewerbung in ENGLISHER SPRACHE, unter Angabe Ihres frühestmöglichen Eintrittstermins, richten Sie bitte anHelen Doron Learning Centre Aschaffenburg, z.H. Manuela Weigl, Haidebachstr. 1, 63808 Haibachodersenden Sie diese als PDF-Datei (max. 4 MB) an: aschaffenburg@helendoron.de (https://mailto:aschaffenburg@helendoron.de)Weitere Informationen über unser Learning Centre und Helen Doron finden Sie unter: https://helendoron.de/haibachaschaffenburg/ (https://helendoron.de/haibachaschaffenburg/)Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Bewerbung!Translation:We are looking for a permanentEnglish teacherpart-timeThe current location is the Learning Centre at Haidebachstraße 1 in Haibach. With Helen Doron, our Learning Centre offers courses for babies, children and teens in English and Spanish, which are ranked No. 1 worldwide. Our Learning Centre currently teaches 150 children of all ages, from 3 months to 19 years. The centre is spacious and modern. Our mission is to support families who wish to educate their children in more than one language and to offer these children an extended language home where they can learn English and/or Spanish with joy and without any pressure to perform, with fun and games. Specially trained teachers use new methods to prepare and implement our teaching content in an age-appropriate way. And with great success!Your tasks with us:- As a Helen Doron English teacher, you will initially teach 2-5 lessons per week, depending on your flexibility and experience in the classroom. The number of hours will increase after 6 months depending on your development and needs.- Depending on your qualifications, you can teach a wide range of specialised English courses to a wide range of age groups (from 3 months to 19 years)- You will teach each of your groups once a week. jobs.description: ...you're in the middle of itThe position is embedded in EU-MIC (European Coalition for Mental Health Medicines Innovation) , a strategic initiative led by the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology (ECNP) . jobs.employer_name: Deutsche Sammlung von Mikrooganismen und Zellkulturen (DSMZ)
jobs.description: The Leibniz Institute DSMZ-German Collection of Microorganisms and Cell Cultures GmbH, Braunschweig offers the position starting January 1, 2027 for aSoftware Developer for the MediaDive Database (m/f/d)**The position has a salary level according to TV-L (https://oeffentlicher-dienst.info/c/t/rechner/tv-l/west?id=tv-l-2023&matrix=1) 13 and is part of the NFDI4Microbiota project (https://nfdi4microbiota.de/ (https://nfdi4microbiota.de/) ). It is initially limited to 2 years and is offered as full time (39.8 hours per week). The position is located in Braunschweig and is not suitable for full remote work.MediaDive (https://mediadive.dsmz.de/) is the world's largest database for cultivation media, providing standardized recipes and growth conditions for thousands of microorganisms. It serves as a vital resource for microbiologists worldwide. The further development of MediaDive is embedded in the NFDI4Microbiota consortium (https://nfdi4microbiota.de/), which is part of the German National Research Data Infrastructure (NFDI). The consortium's mission is to support the microbiological research community by providing access to data, analysis tools, and standards according to the FAIR principles.As a developer for MediaDive, you will be responsible for maintaining, expanding, and modernizing the web application, APIs, and underlying database infrastructure. Together with the DSMZ team of biologists and software engineers, as well as partners within the NFDI4Microbiota consortium, you will develop new features and align services with the needs of the microbiological research community.Your responsibilities:- Further development of the MediaDive web application, backend, and RESTful API- Expanding data standardization, ontology integration, and FAIRness of cultivation data within the framework of the NFDI4Microbiota project- Coordinate the development of MediaDive with other resources of the DSMZ Digital Diversity platform and external NFDI services- Developing user-friendly tools for recipe calculation, media prediction, and data visualizationYour profile:- Master’s degree (or equivalent) in computer science, bioinformatics, or a related field- Strong programming skills in backend and frontend web development- Experience with document and relational databases- Experience with version control (Git), Linux environments, and containerization (Docker)- Interest in microbiological data, data standardization (FAIR principles), and ontologies is beneficial- Accuracy, quality-orientation, and a structured way of working - Intrinsic motivation and team-spirit- Fluent in English / knowledge of German is beneficial- Willingness to undertake occasional business travel (e.g., to NFDI4Microbiota consortium meetings)We offer:- An interdisciplinary working environment with frequent exchange of experience- Participation in building a national research data infrastructure (NFDI)- Motivated colleagues and a pleasant working atmosphere in a scientific area- Further development and support of scientific data services at the DSMZ- Plenty of room for creativity & challenging topics- Opportunities for further education and training- An employer certified according to audit berufundfamilie®, therefore flexible possibilities to combine work and family life.The position is located in Braunschweig and requires a substantial amount of on-site work. Mobile office work is possible for up to 3 days per week.About the DSMZ and new biodata infrastructure DSMZ Digital Diversity:The Leibniz-Institute DSMZ-German Collection of Microorganisms and Cell Cultures establishes an integrated suite of scientific databases of fundamental relevance for life sciences. The databases include BRENDA, SILVA, LPSN, BacDive** and TYGS which are developed in a highly coordinated manner. A dedicated team of 22 scientists and software engineers creates a research data infrastructure which will significantly improve the access to curated and standardized biological data. The resulting data platform DSMZ Digital Diversity will provide an integrated resource and will allow to link and comprehensively analyze the different types of scientific data from all domains of life sciences. For more information visit hub.dsmz.de (https://hub.dsmz.de/) .The DSMZ is funded by the State of Lower Saxony and the German Federal government and is a member of the Leibniz Association. The DSMZ strives to increase the proportion of female scientists and encourages female candidates to apply. At the same time, we are committed to reflecting the diversity of society. We therefore warmly welcome all applications, regardless of gender, cultural or social background, religion, beliefs or sexual identity. Disabled applicants with identical technical and personal qualifications will be preferentially selected. In the case of degrees obtained abroad, proof of equivalence with a German degree must be enclosed. For further information, please refer to the website of the Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB). The DSMZ is an equal opportunity employer, supports balanced work-life career development, and holds the certificate of the audit berufundfamilie®.For further information please contact Lorenz Reimer (lorenz.reimer@dsmz.de (https://mailto:lorenz.reimer@dsmz.de) ). Please send your complete application documents including a CV, motivation letter, copies of certificates, and (if applicable) links to software projects/GitHub with application number 11/26 as a single pdf file to bewerbung@dsmz.de (https://mailto:bewerbung@dsmz.de) (max. 10 MB). Applications are welcome in English or German and will be accepted on a rolling basis so early applicants are encouraged! The deadline for this application is 20.11.2026.Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

jobs.occupation: Research Software Engineer (all genders) HPC & Pferformance Portability (Softwareentwickler/in)
jobs.description: The German Climate Computing Centre (DKRZ) is the central simulation and data processing facility for the German climate and Earth system modelling community and one of the leading institutions in this field worldwide. DKRZ not only operates supercomputers of the highest performance class and one of the largest data and archive systems, but also participates in many national and international projects aimed at improving the software and infrastructure for climate modelling. Here we are offering a position asResearch Software Engineer (all genders) HPC & Performance PortabilityYour tasksA key focus for DKRZ is the development of the climate and weather model ICON, and its further preparation for current and future HPC systems. Within the European PHOENIX project, we aim to develop a maintainable, performance-portable version of ICON that runs efficiently on heterogeneous CPU and GPU architectures. In this context, you will contribute to the development, integration, and optimisation of ICON on the largest European supercomputers.Your work will focus on several aspects of performance-portable scientific software, depending on your background and interests. This includes integrating ICON components based on different programming approaches, such as C++/Kokkos, DaCe, and gt4py, improving their interoperability, and enabling efficient execution on different HPC architectures, particularly NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, but also possible future compute architectures.Further areas of work include improving ICON's efficiency and scalability at very high spatial resolutions. You may also explore the use of mixed precision and AI-oriented hardware features for climate models, or improve the efficient concurrent execution and coupling of ICON with other components. The specific focus of your work will be determined together with the project team, allowing complementary contributions to the different development tasks.Qualifications / Experiences● Academic degree in computer science, applied mathematics, computational physics/engineering, or a related field with a clear focus on scientific computing● Experience in high-performance computing, performance portability, and optimising scientific applications for modern hardware● Experience with scientific software development, ideally involving large, collaboratively developed applications● Programming experience with Fortran or C/C++, ideally in the context of scientific or parallel applications● Experience with parallel programming, for example MPI or GPU programming● Familiarity with performance-portable programming approaches such as DaCe, gt4py, or similar technologies is an advantage● Programming experience under Unix/Linux, including scripting languages such as Python or Bash; experience with HPC environments, performance analysis, or code optimisation is an advantage● Motivation to support open, collaborative, and community-oriented software development● Very good communication skills and knowledge of EnglishEmployment conditionsWe offer work in interdisciplinary teams and excellent connections to national and international research networks. In addition to specific development goals and requirements from our project partners, your work will be characterised by the freedom to explore and implement solutions at the interface between high-performance computing, scientific software engineering, and Earth system modelling. Participation in international conferences, project meetings, and hackathons provides opportunities for further training, exchange with the international HPC community, and presentation of your own results wherever meaningful.We are based in Hamburg, but want to create a suitable working environment by offering flexible working hours and location (up to 100% work from home within Germany). Remuneration will be based on the candidate's qualifications according to TVöD-Bund. You can ideally start already in February 2027, but the exact starting date can be agreed individually. The position is financed by third-party funded projects and is limited until the end of 2029.Interested applicants are requested to compile a single pdf document containing a cover letter, a detailed CV and any additional documents (e.g. professional references). Applications must be submitted via the portal https://dkrz.softgarden.io/de/vacancies.Application deadline : Priority will be given to applications received by 30 November 2026.Questions? Dr. Jan Frederik Engels (engels@dkrz.de) and Dr. Hendryk Bockelmann (bockelmann@dkrz.de) will be happy to answer them in advance.

You don't just oversee compliance – you actively get your hands dirty solving the technical problems that stand between an idea and a certified aircraft.You lead our Engineering, Development, and Certification functions, coordinate external Compliance Verification Engineers, and act as the technical interface to the independent Head of Airworthiness, ensuring robust oversight, clear accountability, and the highest standards of regulatory compliance. You act like an entrepreneur: you take ownership of problems end-to-end, cut through complexity, and drive pragmatic solutions rather than waiting for someone else to decide.ResponsibilitiesRegulatory and Design Assurance Responsibilities- Establish, maintain, and continuously improve the documented Design Assurance System — hands-on, not just on paper.- Ensure that all design work is undertaken in accordance with the Design Assurance System, BCAR A8-21, and other applicable airworthiness regulations.- Ensure that all design activities remain within the scope of the company's approved design privileges.- Ensure that for all design work, compliance with the applicable type certification basis or equivalent is properly demonstrated and verified.- Ensure that flight testing is carried out in accordance with regulatory requirements.- Sign Declarations of Compliance after satisfactory verification of compliance with applicable airworthiness requirements.- Confirm that all design procedures specified in the Design Organisation Exposition have been followed by signing a Declaration of Compliance for each type approval, type certification, design change, or repair design.Organisational and Management Responsibilities- Lead and manage the Engineering, Development, and Certification functions of the Design Organisation, staying close to the technical detail rather than managing from a distance.- Manage and coordinate external Compliance Verification Engineers.- Provide technical oversight and interface to the independent Head of Airworthiness function.- Ensure qualification, competency, and training of engineering and certification personnel.- Coordinate and manage design, development, certification, and flight test programmes with internal and external stakeholders.- Provide strong project management across design, development, certification, and flight test programmes — planning, scheduling, and managing resources with internal and external stakeholders to keep programmes on time and on budget.- Provide technical authority for design decisions, certification strategies, and design changes, personally stepping in when problems get stuck between departments.- Ensure complete, controlled, and traceable design documentation for certification, production, continued airworthiness, and future investigations.- Provide technical support to production, quality, customer support, and incident investigations where required.- Actively identify inefficiencies and gaps in existing processes and drive their resolution with an entrepreneurial, get-it-done mindset.Required Qualifications- Degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering, or a comparable technical qualification.- Extensive professional experience in a regulated industrial environment; experience gained within a German company as well as senior-level experience from the automotive industry are highly desirable.- Proven track record in leading engineering teams, driving technical decisions, and taking full accountability for results, timelines, and compliance.- Strong and practical expertise in complex systems engineering, including electrical and avionics integration.- Solid experience with regulatory frameworks and compliance environments (e.g. DULV BUT, BCAR Section T, UK CAA, FAA, CAAC).- A true problem solver: someone energized rather than deterred by open, unresolved technical challenges, who finds pragmatic paths forward instead of waiting for perfect conditions.- Hands-on, execution-focused leadership style with a high level of assertiveness and decision-making authority — someone who rolls up their sleeves rather than delegating every difficult problem.- Ability to challenge existing structures, enforce standards, and drive implementation across interfaces (Engineering, Certification, Production, Quality).- High level of ownership, resilience, and confidence when operating in complex, regulated, and time-critical environments.- An intrapreneurial mindset: you treat the Design Organisation as if it were your own venture, take initiative beyond the formal job description, and are comfortable building and improving processes rather than just following them.- English, German & Chinese: mandatory (written and spoken).Benefits- Dynamic working environment with the global leader in gyroplane manufacturing.- Comprehensive onboarding and continuous training opportunities.- Supportive and international team culture.- Flexible working hours (flexitime) to support work–life balance.- Corporate fitness programme (Hansefit).- Employer contributions to the pension scheme.- Employee discounts via our corporate benefits platform.- Regular company events that strengthen team spirit.- Free daily lunch at our headquarter.- Overtime compensation and additional paid leave for special occasions.- Unique aviation experience – including a gyrocopter sightseeing flight.Are you ready for an exciting career in aviation? Then join AutoGyro GmbH.We are the world market leader in the development, production and sale of gyrocopters and work with partners in more than 40 countries. Our headquarters and production facility are located at Hildesheim Airport. With state-of-the-art technologies, a high degree of vertical integration and a clear vision for sustainable aviation, we are actively shaping the future.Since our foundation in 1999, we have grown steadily and now employ an international team of nearly 100 qualified specialists and engineers. Through our global sales network, we are consistently pursuing our goal: to bring the thrill of flying, maximum safety and the versatile applications of the Gyro to people all over the world.

PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d): Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as of 01 January2027:PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d):Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementitel (m/f/d)(Part-Time)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: PhD position (65%) / PostDoc (up to 60%)Type of contract: Temporary, limited to 4 years, until 31.12.20230Remuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E 13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.As part of the Centre, the group “Global Land Systems and Biodiversity” takes a system perspective on how production, trade and consumption of food and other biomass products affect ecosystems and people.The VEBITA project, conducted jointly by SGN, the Marburg University and the Institute for Social-Ecological Research (ISOE) brings together researchers and practice partners to work towards utilizing animal movement data for early-warning systems for nature conservation. By analyzing GPS and sensor data from animals with statistical and AI-based methods, VEBITA aims to detect how animal behaviors change in response to land use, climate change, habitat loss, infrastructure development, and other environmental pressures.The adverstised position focuses on the effects of livestock management on wildlife movements contributes a use-case for state-of-the art animal movement data. Currently, livestock keeping has the largest spatial footprint of all land uses and the global biomass of mammalian livestock exceeds that of all remaining wild mammals by an order of magnitude. How and where livestock are kept greatly impacts the movements of the remaining wild mammals.In this context, we seek to develop a refined biodiversity footprint approach that captures how different livestock management strategies impact movement of wild mammals and how management can be adapted to achieve more sustainable outcomes. This subproject is part of VEBITA’s transdisciplinary focus, and the design of the novel footprint approach will consider perspectives of different relevant societal stakeholder groups such as livestock farmers, conservationists, and regulators. Results and insights of this work will also feed back to international science-policy debates on how conservation and human activities can be aligned in the future.Your tasks- Advance existing biodiversity footprint approaches in the context of livestock production and wildlife movement- Classify global livestock management systems- Analyze global patterns of how livestock keeping influences movements of wild mammals- Actively engage in exchange and cooperation within VEBITA’s inter- and transdisciplinary project team- Participate in project meetings and contribute to project reporting- Publish results in international journals in cooperation with the project teamYour profile- MSc degree (or equivalent) for application for a PhD position or PhD degree for application as postdoctoral researcher in a relevant field, e.g., sustainability science, physical geography, ecology or another relevant field- Programming skills (R, Python or similar), familiarity in working with heterogenous datasets and their analysis- Excellent English language skills- Interest in working in an inter- and transdisciplinary project- Interest in applied science at the science-policy interfaceDesirable skills- Experience with stakeholder interactionsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application as a single PDF by 19 November 2026, stating the reference number Ref. #11-26021, including:- cover letter describing your motivation to apply for this position- detailed CV- contact details of two potential references- all academic credentials and certificatesPlease submit your application via our online application system. If you are viewing this vacancy on an external job platform, please visit our careers page and apply via the corresponding "Apply" button. Applications submitted by email cannot be considered.If you have any specific questions about the position, please contact Prof. Dr. Thomas Kastner at thomas.kastner@senckenberg.de.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact xxxxx atvorname.nachname@senckenberg.deFor data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/Please visit our website at www.senckenberg.de for further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung.Application documents will also be made available to members of the selection committee from Marburg University and the Institute for Social-Ecological Research (ISOE), solely for the purpose of assessing applications and selecting candidates.

Senckenberg – Leibniz Institution for Biodiversity and Earth System Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at its Department of River Ecology and Conservation in Gelnhausen, starting as soon as possible2 Postdoctoral Researchers (ecologists) (m/f/d)(full-time / part-time)Location: GelnhausenEmployment scope: full-time / part-time options are availableType of contract: limited two years / an extension is be possibleRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) E 13Senckenberg is one of the world’s leading research institutions in the field of Biodiversity and Earth System Research, with eight research institutes and three natural history museums across Germany and scientists from over 40 nations. Our headquarter is located in the thriving commercial metropolis of Frankfurt in the heart of Germany, which also hosts one of our most famous facilities, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum. The location of the available position is in a Senckenberg institute about 40 kilometers east of Frankfurt in Gelnhausen, a historic town accessible via public transport (rail and bus).We are looking for enthusiastic ecologists with a background in broad-scale biodiversity change, community ecology, macroecology, metacommunities, and/or analysis of ecological time series.The two positions are embedded in one or more of the following projects:1. Synthesis Center on Freshwater Biodiversity Change in Europe The Synthesis Center brings together and supports a broad variety of researchers and practitioners investigating a broad variety of fundamental and applied ecological questions, with a particular focus on broad-scale and long-term biodiversity change, community ecology, freshwater ecology, time series analyses, multiple stressor impacts, and conservation (see doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06400-1 for an example). Data for > 30,000 freshwater biodiversity time series across 30 European countries have already been compiled from rivers and lakes, covering invertebrates, fish, macrophytes, diatoms, and benthic algae, in collaboration with a large pan-European network of > 200 researchers. Positions involved in this project are expected to pursue similar questions using the already available data.2. EU Horizon Europe project BEAGLE (started on 1st October 2026)BEAGLE (Biodiversity methods for advanced monitoring at large scales) is an EU-funded project using new technology to enhance biodiversity monitoring across terrestrial, freshwater, and marine environments. Specifically, the project uses sensors, environmental DNA (eDNA) and AI, as well as citizen science to collect large-scale and high-quality biodiversity data across a consortium of 17 partners. Positions involved in this project will focus on several tasks, including European-scale biodiversity data mobilization activities (e.g., tracking down datasets and preparing them for use), and the learning and deployment of field-based methods for data collection (e.g., Malaise traps). Participating researchers will gain experience in broad-scale biodiversity data collection and management, biodiversity monitoring, and participation in European-scale research networks.Your tasks• Contributing scientifically to one or more of the above-described projects (you can indicate a preference in your application if you have one)• Analyzing spatial and temporal biodiversity data, and accompanied environmental data, to elucidate spatial patterns and temporal trends and drivers thereof• Preparing scientific manuscripts• Attending project meetings and preparing project reports• Mentoring graduate students• Giving oral presentations at national and international conferences• Attending virtual and physical project meetingsYour profile• PhD in Ecology or a related field• Solid background in fields related to the above expected tasks for a given project or projects.• Advanced skills in statistical analyses, using R• Skills in project management and report writing are preferred but not essential• Strong publication record for your current career level• Excellent written and oral communication and project presentation skills in EnglishWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter outlining your suitability for the post, a detailed CV, contact details of 2 references, a list of publications and acquired funding electronically (as a single PDF) stating the **reference #04-26004 by November 22nd, 2026 **using the application form on our website https://www.senckenberg.de/de/karriere/ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt a.M.If you have any specific questions about this role position, please contact Prof. Dr. Peter Haase at peter.haase@senckenberg.de.

jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as soon as possible:PostDoc (m/f/d) in Data-Driven Social Ecological Research(Full-Time / Part-Time** **options available)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: Full-Time; Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, limited to 3 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.SBiK-F has strong cooperations with the Institute for social-ecological research (ISOE) and the position will work closely with both institutions.The position develops quantitative approaches to (1) better characterize and measure human–nature interactions, or (2) use these analyses to identify leverage points for more effective stewardship or monitoring of nature under climate change.Your tasks- Develop quantitative approaches to measure and analyze human–nature interactions- Integrate multiple data streams (ecological, social, remote-sensing, citizen-science) into coherent models of social-ecological system dynamics- Identify leverage points where intervention or monitoring most effectively supports biodiversity- Advance biodiversity or stewardship monitoring frameworks to better incorporate social dimensions- Publish in leading international journals- Contribute to and connect with ongoing research at SBiK-F- Collaborate across the natural- and social-science groups at Senckenberg, ISOE, and partner institutionsYour profile- PhD in ecology, environmental science, quantitative social science, or a related field- Demonstrated experience working with empirical ecological data and preferably also social data- Strong proficiency in R (and/or comparable statistical/programming environments)- Excellent quantitative and statistical skills- Strong publication record in international peer-reviewed journals- Fluency in written and spoken EnglishDesirable skills- Experience with integrating heterogeneous data streams (eg. ecological, social, remote sensing or citizen science data)- Familiarity with AI/ML methods- Track record of interdisciplinary collaboration across natural and social sciences- Experience in quantitative social science methods and working with social or socio-economic data- Experience in acquiring third-party funding- Familiarity with trait-based approaches to social-ecological questions- Familiarity with adaptive capacity and resilience of social-ecological systems- Familiarity with impacts of climate change on the interactions between biodiversity and societyWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV with full publication list, copies of certificates and diplomas, along with the names of two referees), electronically (as a single PDF) stating the reference: #11-26026 by 29.11.2026.Please submit your application via our online application system. If you are viewing this vacancy on an external job platform, please visit our careers page and apply via the corresponding "Apply" button. Applications submitted by email cannot be considered.Please be aware, application documents will also be made available to members of the selection committee from the Institute for Social-Ecological Research (ISOE), solely for the purpose of assessing applications and selecting candidates.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Prof. Dr. Thomas Müller atThomas Müller.For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/Please visit our website at www.senckenberg.de for further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung.

jobs.description: Create your own happiness!Are you a passionate early childhood educator (m/f/d)? Do you put your heart and soul into your work, but haven’t been satisfied with your working conditions so far?Come check us out—maybe you’ll like what you find here?What you can look forward to…The basics: pay, vacation time, and working hours.We are actually offering a fixed-term full-time position. The full-time workweek is 38 hours. Initially, the contract would be fixed-term, but an extension is possible.Pay is based on the TVöD SuE collective bargaining agreement and depends on your professional experience and qualifications. A 13th month’s salary (at 100%, instead of 85%) is paid after one year of service. We have between 32 and 34 days of vacation per year. Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve are paid holidays. The cost of an HVV/Deutschlandticket is fully covered, and if interested, you can participate in a fitness program.The Position: Responsibilities and Working Conditions.We are looking for at least one new early childhood educator with a perfect command of the English language.Your responsibilities include the attentive care, nurturing, and support of the children (age 1-6) entrusted to us in line with our educational approach, working closely with the children, parents, and the entire team. In your daily work, you would speak mainly English.We would appreciate at least some experience in this field and a preference for this age group would be advantageous.Our working conditions are truly worth highlighting: In the elementary section, four colleagues together care for 35 children; in the nursery section, four additional colleagues care for 16 children. In addition, we employ a housekeeping staff member with educational qualifications and, in the future, a substitute.We hold weekly team meetings to discuss weekly schedules, activities, and specific situations, as well as to plan parent-teacher conferences and developmental meetings. Our sponsoring organization places great emphasis on providing good working conditions.The Team: One for all, all for one!Some of us have been working together successfully and happily for over ten years. It goes without saying that we support one another and treat each other with care. Our sense of humor and our willingness to stand up for one another carry us through the sometimes hectic daily routine of the daycare center.On concept days, we discuss educational topics, engage in professional development, and reflect on our work. Regular weekly team meetings, preparation time, and supervision are just as much a part of our routine as extended get-togethers during company outings and Christmas parties.Has this piqued your curiosity? Then you should definitely keep reading…Important: Empathy, joy, and qualifications.To ensure we comply with legal requirements, it is very important that our new team member holds a completed, state-recognized qualification as an early childhood educator (m/f/d), a degree in early childhood education or early childhood development, or a degree as a social pedagogue (m/f/d). It would be helpful if you have a good understanding of the English language, as we are a bilingual facility.We are looking for an empathetic person with a Reggio Emilia approach (including a child-centered perspective) and someone who genuinely enjoys working with children, because we want you to look forward to coming to work.Feel free to get to know us!The Daycare Center: Location. Concept. Focus Areas.The daycare center is located in the heart of Planten un Blomen and is surrounded by plenty of greenery. It is easily accessible by public transportation from all parts of Hamburg (Gänsemarkt, Dammtor, Stephansplatz).There are two groups, a nursery group and an elementary group, in which 42-48 children are currently cared for by nine early childhood educators. Our facilities allow us to organize various projects and activities in workshops and specialized rooms.The foundation of our concept is the Reggio approach. Above all, it reflects our attitude toward others and how we wish to approach life’s changes. Our daycare is a place for self-directed, holistic learning, and we foster a respectful approach not only toward the children entrusted to us, but toward all people.We integrate key areas such as yoga, woodworking, art studio work, language development, music, relaxation and movement, and preschool preparation into our daily routine. Do you have a particular focus? A passion? Let’s find out together if we can integrate this into our daily routine as well…Start up initiative: Kindertagesstätte an der Bucerius Law School e.V.Our small operator, “Kindertagesstätte an der Bucerius Law School e.V.”, was founded in 2008 and is a member of the Paritätischer Wohlfahrtsverband Hamburg. Loki Schmidt was the founding patron of our daycare center.Our organization consists of a single facility. This means that decisions can be made and implemented quickly, easily, and on an individual basis. Here, people are still allowed to be people; they are heard and are not just a personnel number.As a member of the Bucerius family and an initiative of the ZEIT STIFTUNG BUCERIUS, our work makes an important contribution to promoting an open, democratic society.The Future: Do you think we’re a good fit for you?Then please send us your application materials. We would love to get to know you.If you’re interested, feel free to check out our website (https://www.law-school.de/services/kita (https://www.law-school.de/services/kita) ) or our Instagram account (kita.buceriuslaw).Thank you for your attention, and we hope to see you soon!

jobs.description: Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX projectSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN) , headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position in the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Center (SDMC) at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as soon as possible:Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project(Full-Time / Part-Time)Location: FrankfurtEmployment scope: Full-Time / Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, initially limited to 2 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E11- E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Within the TETTRIX project, the position will develop a web-based, open-access biodiversity mapping and Species Distribution Modelling (SDM) platform that enables reproducible data and modelling workflows and transforms biodiversity data into actionable knowledge for biodiversity monitoring and conservation. sound REST API design.- Experience with SQL/PostgreSQL; PostGIS and web-mapping libraries (MapLibre GL, Leaflet, OpenLayers) are a strong plus.- Experience with cloud-based data infrastructure, particularly AWS services (S3, Batch).- Knowledge of columnar data storage and lakehouse technologies (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask).- Experience with data pipelines, batch processing and the integration of large-scale datasets.- Knowledge of hybrid infrastructure architectures and the integration of cloud-based and on-premises services.- Experience with Docker, Git and CI/CD.- Very good command of English.- Willingness to work on site in Frankfurt (up to 40% remote work is possible).Desirable skills- Familiarity with open-access biodiversity databases such as the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS), Darwin Core standards, and biodiversity data life cycles- Familiarity with species distribution modelling and associated statistical/machine-learning approaches (e.g. GLM/GAM, MaxEnt, Random Forest)- A track record in scientific publications, reproducible scientific computing, or open-source projectsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. The Max Planck Society is Germany's premier research organization. The 86 Max Planck Institutes conduct research at highest levels, in the service of the general public, in the natural sciences, life sciences, social sciences, and the humanities.The Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD) is located at the Science Campus Hamburg-Bahrenfeld and investigates dynamical phenomena within matter down to the elementary timescales of atomic and electronic motions, the femtosecond or attosecond timescale. The focus is on the use of short wavelength ultrafast probes, such as X-rays or electron pulses, which are capable of measuring atomic and electronic structures in matter of all kinds.The MPSD currently consists of five scientific departments focusing on solid state physics and theoretical methods in these fields. The MPSD is a partner in the Center for Free-Electron Laser Science (CFEL), collaborating with the Deutsches Elektronen Synchrotron (DESY), European XFEL (EuXFEL) and the University of Hamburg in the development of science based on the X-ray Free Electron Lasers (XFELs).To strengthen our support for experimental research, the MPSD is seeking a highly motivatedElectronics Engineer (m/f/d)Your positionAs an Electronics Engineer, you will support cutting-edge experimental physics research by developing reliable, high-performance electronic systems in close collaboration with scientists, engineers and technical staff.- Develop, design and implement analogue and digital electronic systems for experimental physics applications.- Translate scientific and technical requirements into robust electronic concepts, circuits and complete devices.- Design, assemble, commission and test printed circuit boards (PCBs) and electronic instruments, from initial concept through prototyping to deployment in the laboratory.- Diagnose, troubleshoot and optimise existing electronic systems and measurement equipment.- Develop firmware for microcontrollers and support the integration of hardware, firmware and software components.- Work closely with researchers and engineers to provide practical, user-oriented technical solutions for a broad range of experimental setups.- Prepare and maintain technical documentation, including circuit diagrams, PCB layouts, assembly instructions and test procedures.- As the role involves hands-on development, assembly, testing and support of laboratory equipment, regular on-site presence is an essential part of the position.Your background and skills- A university degree (Master’s degree or Diplom) in electrical engineering, electronics or a closely related field.- Sound practical experience in the development of analogue and digital electronic systems, including circuit design, PCB layout and the assembly, commissioning and testing of electronic devices.- Proficiency in common ECAD tools for schematic capture and PCB design, ideally including KiCad or Autodesk EAGLE, as well as familiarity with circuit-simulation tools.- Knowledge of firmware development for microcontrollers, ideally using C/C++. Experience in developing user software for the control, operation and monitoring of electronic devices is also desirable.- Experience with FPGA development and VHDL is an advantage. Familiarity with CAD systems for mechanical design is also desirable.- A strong understanding of the requirements and working practices of a diverse scientific and technical environment, combined with intercultural competence and effective communication skills.- Excellent written and spoken German and English skills.- Experience in laboratory electronics, measurement technology, scientific instrumentation or experimental physics is desirable.Our offer- A varied and responsible position in an international and interdisciplinary scientific environment, with the opportunity to contribute directly to innovative experimental research.- Close collaboration with scientists, engineers and technical staff on challenging and diverse technical projects.- A family-friendly working environment with flexible working arrangements, in line with the practical requirements of laboratory-based work.- Opportunities for professional development and further training.- Attractive remuneration and social benefits in accordance with the applicable public-sector collective agreement, depending on qualifications and professional experience.- An initial contract for two years, with the possibility of permanent employment thereafter.- The opportunity to work in a collaborative, inclusive and forward-looking research environment.- A subsidy for the Profiticket as a Germany ticketYour applicationThe Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. Airbus bietet moderne und treibstoffeffiziente Verkehrsflugzeuge sowie dazugehörige Dienstleistungen an. Airbus ist auch führend in Europa im Bereich Verteidigung und Sicherheit und eines der größten Raumfahrtunternehmen der Welt. Im Bereich Hubschrauber stellt Airbus die weltweit effizientesten Lösungen und Dienstleistungen für zivile und militärische Hubschrauber bereit.Job descriptionIn order to support the Robotics and Automation department, CTC GmbH is looking for anIntern within Robot-based Continuous Ultrasonic Welding (d/f/m)Are you looking for an internship or thesis? Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Airbus Operations Subsidiary CTC GmbH as an intern (d/f/m)!- Location: Stade- Start: April 2026- Duration: 6 monthsFor CTC GmbH in Stade, we are looking for students for practical assignments (internships), the topic can subsequently be continued in the form of a bachelors or master thesis. The CTC GmbH is a wholly owned subsidiary of Airbus Operations GmbH. CTC is Germany's leading centre for research and development in the field of design and production of large and complex CFRP components; with an international reputation as an expert for process development, series readiness and production optimisation. The focus of the CTC's work is the development of series technologies for the production and assembly of CFRP components in aircraft construction. In the CTC, you can contribute to various projects in your area of focus and have a great deal of creative freedom. We look forward to receiving your application!Your locationYou work at the Stade location. Experience the special flair south of the Elbe in your free time, close to the cosmopolitan culture of Hamburg.Your benefits- Work-life balance with a 35-hour week (flexitime) and EUR 750 gross/monthly salary.- A final thesis is possible after consultation with the department.- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.- Work with modern/diversified technologies.- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.Your tasks and responsibilities- Conduct literature research on continuous ultrasonic welding, industrial robots and their interactions and support in the ongoing welding activities.- Analysis of requirements and preparation of specifications for the new welding end effector.- Redesign of the new end effector using CATIA and performing static and dynamic structural simulations to validate the design.- Iterative improvement of the structure and validation of the model under measured forces (static, dynamic, frictional, etc.) from the process.- Ensure proper documentation and knowledge transfer for the continued development of the system.Desired skills and qualifications- Enrolled full-time student (d/f/m) in the area of mechanical, mechatronics, electrical, automation or manufacturing engineering, aerospace engineering or an equivalent field of study.- Knowledge in the field of electronics and sensors.- Experience with CAD software especially CATIA.- Experience with structural analysis (static and dynamic).- Ability to work independently and on your own responsibility.- High intrinsic motivation, teamwork and communication skills.- Language skills: Very good English and preferably good German skills.Please upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrollment certificate.Not a 100% match? No worries! jobs.description: About usAirbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Airbus is also a European leader in defence and security and one of the world's leading space businesses. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.Job descriptionIn order to support the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics department, Airbus Operations is looking for aMaster student (d/f/m) in the field of Aerodynamics in the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics departmentYou are looking for a master thesis and want to get to know the work of a job title? Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics department as a master student (d/f/m)!- Location: Hamburg- Start: 01.06.2025- Duration: 6 monthsYour opportunity- Are you passionate about aircraft physics?- Are you keen to master the way we compute external loads acting on the vehicle due to maneuvers, flight in turbulence, landing impact, ground-handling?- Do you like to work in an empowered manner?- Do you enjoy connecting people and collaborating with many different interfaces?- This job will give you the opportunity to work internationally with several internal flight physics departments and with teams located in Europe and India.About usWe are a team of 16 multicultural and passionate engineers who perform the gust calculations for overall aircraft design for all aircraft types. Our team is involved from a very early design stage until certification and also in-service support. We are responsible for running build model activities such as finite element modeling, creating mass and aerodynamics models. We perform gust loads calculation, including failure cases, and deliver to internal interfaces. On top, we are deeply involved in research and technology aspects with new aircraft configuration assessments, model based system engineering, automation and machine learning.IntroductionThe current industry approaches of modeling unsteady aerodynamic flow for the prediction of gust loads typically assume linear flow conditions. Linearity greatly reduces the computational time required to evaluate all the flight points and gust conditions required by the certification specifications (CS-25). At the same time, disregarding non-linearities such as boundary layer separation arising from the high angles of attack induced by strong gusts can lead to an over-estimation of loads and thus to an increased structural weight of the aircraft.Your locationYou will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.Your benefits- Work-life balance with a 35-hour week (flexitime).- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.- Work with modern/diversified technologies.- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.Your tasks and responsibilitiesDuring this six months Master thesis you will develop and evaluate an unsteady aerodynamic model that includes the effect of flow separation in a piecewise linear approach. The model will be built using linearized computational fluid dynamics (CFD) of a complete flexible aircraft and adapted using aerodynamic data obtained in the non-linear flow region at high angles of attack. You will evaluate the model by comparison against higher-fidelity models, such as obtained from non-linear time domain simulation, with respect to gust loads.You will contribute to:- Optimize the design of Airbus commercial aircraft in the frame of new wing technologies- the development of new approaches to model unsteady aerodynamics considering non-linearities for gust loads and flutter computation- Actively support us as a new member of our team on our journeyDesired skills and qualifications- You are a fulltime enrolled master student (d/f/m) within Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or equivalent- You have good knowledge in aerodynamics, CFD and potential flows- Ideally you already have first experience in CFD using TAU or CODA- You have knowledge in coding using Python and/or Matlab- You bring basic knowledge in overall aircraft design and basic competencies in flight loads calculation and flight mechanics- You are passionate to understand physical aspects and to use your engineering judgement- If you are familiar with tools like MSC.NASTRAN or ALTAIR HyperWorks, this is beneficial- You are a highly motivated, proactive and open-minded person with a great sense of initiative- You are keen to deepen your technical knowledge while enjoying to work in a multicultural team- Your English is at negotiating levelPlease upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrollment certificate.Not a 100% match?
