jobs.occupation: Research Associates (m/f/d) in Evolution, Genomics and Cell Biology of Algae (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: The University of Koblenz stands for interdisciplinarity in practice, innovative strength, and a dynamic approach to shaping the future. It makes a decisive contribution to the development of a strong academic and economic region, while also maintaining a strong international presence and network. Its researchers are dedicated to addressing key, socially relevant issues in the four focus areas of education, computer science, culture and communication, and materials and the environment. Approximately 9,800 students benefit from a high-quality, flexible range of academic programs. The university offers its staff attractive working conditions. Join our team and help shape our future! We are seeking, to start as soon as possible, two part-time (65%) fixed-term Research Associates (m/f/d)in Evolution, Genomics and Cell Biology of AlgaeThe position is for 65% of a full-time workload (currently 25.35 hours per week) and is limited to a term of three years. The fixed-term appointment is based on the provisions of the German Act on Fixed-Term Employment Contracts in Academia (WissZeitVG). Further academic qualification (Ph.D.) is part of the job responsibilities and is strongly encouraged. The positions are in the field of evolution, genomics, and cell biology of algae within the Aquatic Ecosystem Analysis research group at the Institute for Integrated Natural Sciences, Biology, in Division 3: Mathematics/Natural Sciences.How do new photosynthetic organelles arise, and how are they permanently integrated into a eukaryotic cell? In a newly discovered photosynthetic single-celled organism, we are investigating an unusually complex plastid whose evolutionary origin and cellular integration have so far remained largely unclear. This system thus offers a rare opportunity to study key processes of the evolution and integration of photosynthetic organelles in a living organism. Preliminary genomic and ultrastructural data suggest that the plastids arose from a complex endosymbiosis with an alga.At the heart of the project is a yet-to-be-named unicellular alga from the Cercozoa. Two closely linked doctoral projects are jointly investigating the evolutionary origin of the plastids. One of the projects focuses on genomic adaptations, while the second, primarily using microscopy, examines the cellular integration and functional properties of the plastids. To this end, we combine modern genomics and phylogenomics with bioinformatic analyses, cell culture, and light and electron microscopy techniques. Among other things, we are investigating the genomes of the host cell and the plastid, the transfer and origin of plastidial genes and proteins, as well as the architecture and inheritance of plastids within the cell. Both positions combine experimental work in the wet lab with the analysis of genomic and microscopic data, offering scope for diverse research focuses in the fields of algae evolution, genomics, and cell biology. The doctoral projects are based in the Aquatic Ecosystem Analysis research group, are closely coordinated, and are designed to last three years. Further information about the research group can be found at www.kennethdumack.de (http://www.kennethdumack.de/) .Your Responsibilities - Advanced scientific training with the goal of earning a Ph.D.- Independent work on a Ph.D. project focusing on the evolution and cellular integration of a complex plastid- Conducting and evaluating genomic, phylogenomic, microscopic, and cell biological studies with a project-specific focus- Cultivation and experimental investigation of unicellular algae, as well as analysis of the data generated- Interpretation and publication of research results in international journals, as well as presentation at scientific conferences- Close collaboration within the joint research project and with national and international partnersYour Profile - A successfully completed graduate degree (Master’s or equivalent) in biology, biochemistry, molecular biology, bioinformatics, or a related field- A strong interest in research questions in the fields of evolution, genomics, and/or cell biology- Experience in at least one of the following areas is an asset: cultivation of microorganisms or algae, molecular biology methods, genomics and bioinformatics, phylogenetics or phylogenomics, or light and electron microscopy- Willingness and interest in independently familiarizing yourself with new experimental or bioinformatics methods- Willingness to travel domestically and internationally for work- Very good written and spoken English skills - An independent, structured, and meticulous approach to work, as well as a high degree of motivation and scientific curiosity- Ability to work well in a team and interest in close collaboration within a joint, interdisciplinary research projectWe offer- An exciting and highly varied scope of responsibilities in a collegial team with open communication structures - Compensation according to Pay Grade 13 of the TV-L - standard public-sector benefits in accordance with TV-L (annual bonus, pension plan (VBL))- Work-life balance, flexible working hours- A diverse sports program with health-promoting activities The University of Koblenz welcomes applications from people of all ages, regardless of gender identity, disability, ethnic or cultural background, religion, worldview, or sexual orientation. We strive to increase the proportion of women in our workforce and are therefore particularly interested in applications from women.In cases of equal qualifications and competence, women will be given preferential consideration if they are underrepresented. People with severe disabilities will be given preferential consideration if their professional and personal qualifications are otherwise equal.For further information, please contact the two project leaders, Prof. Dr. Kenneth Dumack (kenneth.dumack@uni-koblenz.de (https://mailto:kenneth.dumack@uni-koblenz.de) ) and Dr. Jule Freudenthal (jule.freudenthal@uni-koblenz.de (https://mailto:jule.freudenthal@uni-koblenz.de) ).Please submit your complete application materials (cover letter, resume detailing your academic and research background, and copies of relevant degree certificates) by 22.11.2026, citing reference number 110/2026, exclusively via email as a single PDF file to bewerbung@uni-koblenz.de. Please briefly explain in your cover letter which of the two research areas “Evolution and Genomics of Plastids” or “Cell Biology and Microscopic Investigation of Plastid Integration” you are particularly interested in. Applications expressing interest in both research areas are expressly welcome. Please do not submit application photos. Upon completion of the selection process, the application materials will be destroyed in accordance with data protection regulations.

Our preliminary findings indicate that it is also expressed by lung immune cells, where it may contribute to antiviral defense. These findings further suggest that the thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1)/CD47 signaling axis limits hemoglobin expression and its associated antiviral activity.The project aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying hemoglobin-mediated antiviral defense and determine how this response is regulated by TSP-1/CD47 signaling. Combining mechanistic studies with in vivo models, we will explore whether targeting this pathway can enhance antiviral immunity while avoiding excessive inflammation and lung tissue damage.Your Tasks- Perform in vitro and in vivo experiments to characterize the intrinsic and extrinsic (paracrine) functions of hemoglobin in lung immune and epithelial cells- Apply molecular biology techniques- Plan, perform, and analyze therapeutic intervention studies- Present research findings at national and international conferences and contribute to peer-reviewed publications- Assist in supervising Bachelor's/Master's studentsIhr Profil: - You have a university degree (Master or Diploma) in Biology, Molecular Medicine, Immunology, Biochemistry, or a related field- Solid background in cell culture and standard molecular biology techniques- Experience in laboratory animal science (FELASA B) is an advantage- Strong interest in basic research in virology/immunology- Independent, structured, and team-oriented working style- Excellent written and spoken English skills; German language skills are a plus but not requiredFreuen Sie sich auf: - An exciting, methodologically diverse PhD project in an internationally visible research field- Dedicated supervision of the doctoral project within a cooperative working group with regular seminars- State-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure at University Hospital Essen- Enrollment into the Graduate School for Biomedical Science ‘BIOME’ (https://www.uni-due.de/biome (https://www.uni-due.de/biome) )- Salary according to the German public sector pay scale (TV-L, E13, 65%), fixed-term for 3 years- A collegial working environment that encourages independent scientific ideas- Einen sicheren Arbeitsplatz im öffentlichen Dienst des Landes NRW- Faire Bezahlung nach Tarif (TV-L) inkl. We are looking to support our rapidly growing team as soon as possible: Postdoctoral Fellow in Computational Cancer Evolution (f/m/x)Department I of Internal Medicine - CECADYour tasksWe are looking for an ambitious postdoctoral researcher with a proven track record in computational cancer evolution to join our Integrated Cancer Research Laboratory at the CECAD Research Center in Cologne. In this role, you will reconstruct the clonal and subclonal architecture of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and track its evolution under targeted therapies. Using bulk and single-cell sequencing data, you will infer tumour phylogenies and quantify intratumour heterogeneity, subclonal selection and genomic instability (e.g. copy-number alterations, whole-genome doubling and chromothripsis).You will identify evolutionary trajectories leading to treatment resistance, relapse and Richter transformation. Furthermore, you will develop and apply computational methods based on evolutionary principles and integrate genomic, transcriptomic and spatial data with clinical outcomes. Your analyses will link evolutionary features to treatment response, MRD kinetics and survival.For this work, the lab has access to blood and bone marrow samples from more than 900 patients with CLL treated within prospective clinical trials of the German CLL Study Group (GCLLSG), including samples taken before treatment and at relapse, linked to detailed clinical and measurable residual disease (MRD) data.You will lead your own projects, contribute to collaborative projects within the lab and with external partners, and co-supervise PhD and Master students.Your profile• A PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, statistics, physics, computer science or a related field• A proven track record in computational cancer evolution, demonstrated by first-author publications• Hands-on experience in reconstructing clonal and subclonal tumour evolution from sequencing data (e.g. clonal deconvolution, phylogenetic inference, mutational signatures)• Experience in copy-number and structural variant analysis from whole-genome or whole-exome sequencing data; experience with single-cell DNA or RNA sequencing data is a plus• Fluency in Python and/or R, and experience with reproducible workflows (e.g. Snakemake, Nextflow) on high performance computing clusters• Experience with longitudinal or clinical trial data and with haematological malignancies is a plus• Ability to work independently and in close collaboration with clinicians and wet-lab scientists• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spokenOur offer• Everything but ordinary: You can expect a secure job in a challenging, innovative environment – including company pension schemes and regular working hours without business trips.• Work-life balance: Whether full-time or part-time, with or without children – with numerous support options, we will find the right path together.• Team spirit in R(h)ine culture: You will be warmly welcomed by an interdisciplinary team that values mutual respect and helpfulness.• Strong perspectives: We offer extensive training opportunities – so you can continuously grow and set new goals.Your future in detailThe Integrated Cancer Research Laboratory (www.al-sawaf-lab.com), led by Prof Othman Al-Sawaf and based at the CECAD and Department I of Internal Medicine, was founded in 2024 and is funded by a large Emmy-Noether-Grant of the German Research Council (DFG). The focus of the lab is to integrate multimodal analyses to study the plasticity, evolution and prognosis of cancer with a special focus on hematological malignancies. In the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden, researchers from the Social Sciences and Humanities as well as artists explore the relationships between technology, science, and society. The Lab was initiated by The Schaufler Foundation together with TUD Dresden University of Technology. The Lab's guiding theme for the upcoming third funding phase (April 2027–September 2030) is "Energy Cultures in Transition". The guiding theme is investigated from a humanities, cultural, social, and educational science perspective, explored through artistic practice, and communicated to the public. For the third funding phase, the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden comprises eight doctoral fellowships and an annually changing Artist in Residence program.TUD embodies a university culture that is characterized by cosmopolitanism, mutual appreciation, thriving innovation and active participation. For TUD, diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.The Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden offers, subject to the availability of resources, aDoctoral Fellowshipfor a period of 2 years, with the option of extension by 1.5 years, starting on April 1, 2027. The fellowship (EUR 1,850 per month, plus a grant for material costs of EUR 150 and, where applicable, a family supplement of EUR 315 per child) is aimed at early-career researchers in the field of Sociology. Primary supervision will be provided by Prof. Dr. Susann Wagenknecht, Chair of Micro-Sociology and Technosocial Interaction.The guiding theme Energy Cultures in Transition understands energy as a cultural phenomenon deeply inscribed in aesthetic, historical, political, ecological, economic, and socio-technological practices and systems. Building on the dynamically growing research fields of the Energy Humanities, Science & Technology Studies, and the Digital Humanities, the aim is to examine how modern energy regimes—from petromodernity, to nuclear culture, and post-carbon futures—have shaped not only material infrastructures but also subjectivities, power relations, progress narratives, geopolitical orders, ecologies, and knowledge systems, while simultaneously being shaped by them. Interdisciplinary perspectives from the social sciences, cultural studies, humanities, and educational research represented at the Schaufler Kolleg@TU Dresden enable the analysis of the multifaceted entanglements of energy, culture, and society. The focus is on questions concerning the representation, communication, and aesthetics of energy transitions and resource paradigms as well as continuities between resource economies and information economies, the relationships between energy, labor, environment, and consumer culture, and the role of colonialism, gender, nationalism, geopolitics, education, and social justice in deciding energy futures and navigating collective transformation processes. In the field of Sociology, the following research areas and questions are of particular relevance to the guiding theme:- The (conflict-ridden) negotiation of imaginaries, infrastructures, institutional frameworks, and/or externalities (e.g., emissions, waste, waste heat) associated with energy production and supply across a wide variety of practices, communities, networks, organizations, markets, fields, and/or assemblagesTasks:Your tasks include independent research and academic further qualification with the goal of completing a doctorate at TUD, as well as writing a dissertation on a topic within the guiding concept "Energy Cultures in Transition" in the discipline of Sociology. In addition, engagement in the areas of science communication and outreach is expected. Shared office spaces will be made available to the fellows. Participation in the Kolleg's English-language training program is mandatory.Requirements:You hold an excellent university degree in Sociology or a comparable field in the social sciences, as well as relevant previous experience in the sociological analysis of the environment, technology, or energy, and/or in the field of Science and Technology Studies. You have a strong ability to work in teams and enjoy interdisciplinary collaboration. As the training program is conducted in English, you have English skills at a minimum of C1 level. In accordance with the doctoral regulations of the Faculty of Arts, Humanities and Social Science, the dissertation may be written in either German or English—if you choose to write it in German, corresponding German language skills are required. Beyond this, German language skills are desirable but not mandatoryWe offer:The opportunity to pursue a doctorate within the Schaufler Kolleg with a structured qualification program and integration into an interdisciplinary research project. You will receive a fully equipped office workspace on the premises of TUD and access to an excellent research infrastructure, including participation in Research Studios and writing retreats. The Graduate Academy and other central institutions of TUD offer numerous further training and qualification opportunities. In addition, within the limits of the available project funds, the Schaufler Lab will cover the costs of conference travel. Inclusion and equal opportunities are important to us. We therefore look forward to receiving applications from people regardless of gender, origin, sexual orientation, worldview, or disability. TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. Weitere Berufsbezeichnung:Strategische/r Einkäufer/in; Technische/r Einkäufer/inStellenbeschreibung:About usWe see the semiconductor industry as a realm of possibility. We see opportunity. We see the profound impact that our graphene solutions will have in transforming the industry. We invite you to join us in driving change with our fundamentally human-centered approach, uniting bright minds around a shared vision. The vision is: Prove to everybody that you can make a fundamental change. Prove with your knowledge and skills how things can be done differently. Together, we can change the paradigm of how the world connects.About our technologyThe semiconductor industry’s growing demand for more powerful chips with higher bandwidth and lower power finds its solution in our technology. We connect chips to high-throughput, low-delay computing networks. The key lies in harnessing the physical properties of graphene to combine electronic computing with photonic communication, allowing countless chips to interact almost as if they were one. Our graphene photonic innovation increases computing power and efficiency to a new order of magnitude.In short, we connect chips to create powerful and energy-efficient networks, overcoming connectivity limitations in the semiconductor industry. We deliver the graphene solution.The RoleBlack Semiconductor is looking for a Strategic Procurement Manager (f/m/d) or Category Manager (f/m/d) to strengthen our growing team in Aachen, Germany. In this role, you will lead strategic sourcing and supplier management activities for materials critical to semiconductor manufacturing. You will ensure continuity of supply, optimize total cost of ownership, and maintain quality compliance while adapting to evolving technology requirements and market conditions.To join our team, you should be excited to take ownership of:- Develop and execute global sourcing strategies for semiconductor materials, including wafers, photoresists, CMP slurries, specialty gases, chemicals, and other critical materials.- Identify, qualify, and manage strategic suppliers while ensuring alignment with technology roadmaps, quality standards, and production requirements.- Negotiate contracts, pricing, and commercial terms to achieve cost targets while securing reliable supply.- Monitor semiconductor material markets, supplier performance, pricing trends, and supply chain risks to identify opportunities and mitigation strategies.- Collaborate with R&D, process engineering, quality, and manufacturing teams to align material requirements with technology and production needs.- Support new product introductions by sourcing materials that meet emerging process requirements and scalability targets.- Manage procurement performance, supplier relationships, and reporting activities to support business objectives.Your Profile- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in supply chain management, engineering, physics, materials science, business, or a related field.- 5+ years of experience in procurement, strategic sourcing, or supply chain management, preferably within semiconductors, electronics, or advanced manufacturing.- Proven experience negotiating contracts, managing suppliers, and driving cost optimization initiatives.- Strong understanding of semiconductor materials and processes, including wafers, specialty gases, chemicals, photoresists, lithography, etching, and metallization materials.- Strong analytical skills with experience using ERP/procurement systems and data analysis tools.- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills with fluent English; German language skills are considered an advantage.- Willing to work on-site at our Aachen office at least once a week.Our work culturePeople Over Processes. At Black Semiconductor, flexibility is key—we ensure work adapts to life, not the other way around. We champion work-life harmony, where careers are meaningful and enriching. Our processes are human-centric, allowing you to focus on what mattersLet’s grow together. Your potential is our priority. We provide the autonomy to make a lasting impact and nurture your growth through a culture of continuous learning. We invest in your journey for professional and personal developmentYour Health and Future Matter. Your well-being is paramount. We offer a comprehensive benefits package with outstanding insurance, pension and virtual stock options for your mental, physical, and financial health. Your peace of mind is our priority - in the present and futureWe Live Openness. Collaboration and inclusivity are the cornerstones of our culture. We practice openness, fostering trust and respect. Individuality is our collective strength, fueling innovation and driving us forwardWe connect chips – and people. We encourage qualified individuals from any background to apply. We foster an inclusive and supportive work environment that values collaboration, innovation, and growth. Join our team and be part of an organization dedicated to making a difference in the industry.Can you picture yourself in this Role and our Company? Let’s connectIf your application results in an employment relationship, your Applicant Data will be transferred to our personnel records and processed in accordance with applicable legal requirements; otherwise, your Applicant Data will be retained for up to six (6) months after completion of the recruitment process. Read more about our privacy policy here. (https://www.blacksemi.com/privacy-policy)Homeoffice:Umfang: Maximal 70%

Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Your area of responsibility Research topic: Plant immunity Plant pathogens secrete small molecules in their host to manipulate cellular processes and cause disease. Plants are not defenseless, however, and have evolved a wide variety of immune receptors to sense these pathogen-associated molecules and subsequently trigger an immune response to restrict pathogen infection. In the Molecular Plant Immunity research group, we investigate the molecular basis of effector recognition and immune receptor activation, and how evolutionary forces shape these processes. We then leverage this knowledge to develop strategies for sustainable disease resistance in crops. As a foundation under public law, the IPB is under direct supervision of the state of Saxony-Anhalt.The IPB is an internationally recognized research institution and consists of four scientific Departments, additional independent junior research groups, and the Department Administration & Infrastructure (about 200 employees, including about 40 PhD students). Research at the IPB aims to understand the (bio)chemical basis of plant resilience and performance in challenging environments related to climate change. jobs.description: Founded in 1409, Leipzig University is one of Germany’s largest universities and a leader in research and medical training. With around 30,000 students and more than 5000 members of staff across 14 faculties, it is at the heart of the vibrant and outward-looking city of Leipzig. Leipzig University offers an innovative and international working environment as well as an exciting range of career opportunities in research, teaching, knowledge and technology transfer, infrastructure and administration.The Institute for Geography at the Faculty of Physics and Earth System Sciences seeks to fill the above position.The PhD position is part of the project “CASCADE – Cascading impacts of climate extremes: new perspectives for interlinking Earth System Sciences in Leipzig” on compound and cascading impacts of climate extremes. CASCADE investigates how floods and droughts affect society and the environment, combining large-scale data analysis with a systems perspective on human–environment interactions.Our knowledge of the impacts of climate extremes is only as good as the data that record them. The PhD project aims to uncover biases in climate impact databases and research and to provide a more comprehensive view of flood and drought impacts at the global scale. To this end, the doctoral researcher will link and harmonise existing databases (e.g. ROUGE, Wikimpacts, EM-DAT) into a common event, impact and spatial framework, and will contribute to developing a multilingual news-based impact dataset that helps to fill gaps in existing sources. Using independent global hazard and exposure data as a reference, the project will analyse where and for which impacts the sources agree, how reported magnitudes differ, and how the likelihood that an event is recorded at all depends on hazard severity, exposure, socioeconomic conditions, language and media presence.The project benefits from close collaboration with the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ). The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team at the interface of geography, climate-risk research and data science.About the position- Salary group 13  TV-L - Fixed term of 3 years, Qualification-related purposes - 75 % of a full-time position, part-time employment possible- Start date: 1 March 2027The role- Linking and harmonisation of text-based and established impact databases (e.g. ROUGE, Wikimpacts, news-based data, EM-DAT) into a common global event, impact and spatial framework- Comparative analysis of where, when and for which impact types the datasets converge or diverge, using global hazard and exposure data as an independent reference- Analysis of the geographical, socioeconomic and linguistic factors that shape the visibility of impacts in different data sources- Development of a combined, bias-aware global view of flood and drought impacts- Contribution to the development and validation of a multilingual news-based impact dataset using natural language processing (NLP) and large language models (LLMs)- Publication of results in international peer-reviewed journals, presentation at scientific conferences and open publication of code and dataAbout you- University degree (e.g. master’s) or equivalent in geography, computational social sciences, digital humanities, environmental or earth system sciences, disaster risk research or a closely related field- Experience in data analysis, in particular in combining and harmonising heterogeneous datasets, e.g. demonstrated through the master’s thesis, research projects or work experience- Excellent programming skills (e.g. Python, R)- Experience in the analysis of spatial data, e.g. spatial statistics- Interest in climate-risk, natural-hazard or disaster research, e.g. demonstrated through coursework or the master’s thesis- Very good written and spoken English (at least language proficiency level B2)- Experience with, or demonstrable interest in, natural language processing or large language models preferable, e.g. through coursework or projectsWhat we offer you- a varied role with a high degree of responsibility in the dynamic environment of a major university- Collaboration in a friendly, supportive and motivated team- flexible working hours and mobile working to support work-life balance- Goal-oriented staff development throughout your working states (TV-L), including an annual special payment and occupational pension scheme- excellent transport links and the option to purchase a discounted public transport ticket, such as the Deutschlandticket as a commuter pass- a wide range of food options in the refectories and cafés operated by Studentenwerk Leipzig.Leipzig University aims to increase the proportion of women in positions of responsibility and therefore expressly invites qualified women to apply. jobs.description: About GFGlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors that enable AI at scale, from the cloud to the physical world. We partner closely with our customers to deliver differentiated, power-efficient, high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. Across our global footprint in the United States, Europe and Asia, our teams are solving complex challenges that shape the future of technology. At GF, you'll find the opportunity to make an impact, work with world-class talent and contribute to a more secure, sustainable future.Your JobIn semiconductor manufacturing, no processing machine runs continuously yielding the same results. Materials used in the machine can degrade over time, simple factors like –outside temperature can fluctuate, and high usage and low usage play a roll. For stable process results, specific machine settings and recipe parameters are tuned automatically or manually. This is an essential part of work for our process and equipment experts.As a PhD candidate, you will be looking differently at our machines and processes. You already have a scientist´s or an engineer´s view. You know and see the parameters available, regardless of current usage. There, your journey starts towards finding the optimal machine and process settings with as few as possible latest data points. Latest advances in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence indicate the possibility for improvements and will guide your research.The goal of this work shall be the summary and testing of state-of-the-art methods in real-world applications as well as development of new methods tailored to the needs of the semiconductor industry, so in this work Data Science approaches are to be developed to enable process experts to use ML and AI for machine and process tuning.   The contract for this position is set up for 3 years with the possibility to extend it by one additional year, if required. We are looking for a research associate who wants to take a coordinating role in a joint project with other partners from academia and industry and in aligning their research work to the requirements of later mass production. You will systematically document and present the results in regular reports. GF supports the publication of scientific results in leading journals and the protection of intellectual property by the submission of patents.   Required Qualifications- You have completed or are finalizing your Master Thesis in Computer Science, Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Electrical Engineering or a comparable research field.- Your passion is to use your scientific knowledge in a cross-functional team together with experts from other sciences and fields of engineering.- You have already developed your own software, but also have high technical understanding capabilities.- You have solid skills in Python and related Machine Learning libraries.- Wrangling and evaluating data is standard for you.- You know how to use state-of-the-art word processing software to document and communicate your results.- You have a high degree of independence and time flexibility and enjoy communication within global teams.- A good command of written and spoken English (C1) completes your profile.Preferred Qualifications- First insights into semiconductor fabrication processes, e.g. deposition, etching etc. are a plus.- Knowledge about state models, digital twins, predictive control or world models, and about control theory are a plus.- Knowledge of Cloud environments, e.g. AWS, is a plus. Start Date2027, 3 years contract with 40h/week work time.Information about our benefits you can find here: hierSchlagworte: Englisch, RF, EmpfehlungsbundQuelle/Bewerbung via: https://www.empfehlungsbund.de/jobs/309367/phd-on-predictive-process-machine-control (https://www.empfehlungsbund.de/jobs/309367/phd-on-predictive-process-machine-control#apply_form)Kurzinfo zum UnternehmenÜber GFGlobalFoundries (GF) ist ein führender Hersteller von Halbleitern, auf die sich die Welt zum Leben, Arbeiten und Vernetzen verlässt. Wir sind innovativ und arbeiten mit unseren Kunden zusammen, um energieeffizientere und leistungsfähigere Produkte für die Automobilindustrie, intelligente mobile Geräte, das Internet der Dinge (IoT), Kommunikationsinfrastrukturen und andere wachstumsstarke Märkte zu entwickeln.Mit unserem globalen Produktionsnetzwerk, das sich über die USA, Europa und Asien erstreckt, sind wir eine vertrauenswürdige und zuverlässige Quelle für Kunden in aller Welt. Jeden Tag liefert unser talentiertes und vielfältiges Team Ergebnisse mit einem unnachgiebigen Fokus auf Sicherheit, Langlebigkeit und Nachhaltigkeit. GF beschäftigt weltweit rund 13.000 Mitarbeitende, davon 3.000 in Dresden. Weitere Informationen finden Sie unter www.gf.com.

Weitere Berufsbezeichnung:Technische Informatik; Software-Engineering; Künstliche Intelligenz; InformationswissenschaftStellenbeschreibung:As part of the German government's artificial intelligence (AI) strategy, the successful Saxon competence center ScaDS.AI Dresden/Leipzig (Center for Scalable Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence) is being expanded into a leading German AI competence center for Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI). For TUD Dresden University of Technology, diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.At the Center for Interdisciplinary Digital Sciences (CIDS), the Department for Scalable Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence (ScaDS.AI Dresden) offers, subject to the availability of resources, two project positions funded by the BMFTR asResearch Associate / PostDoc (m/f/x)(subject to personal qualification, employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L)starting as soon as possible. The positions are fixed-term until March 31, 2029. The individual contract duration will be determined according to the candidate’s qualifications and the intended academic qualification goal. An extension may be possible subject to the availability of resources. The period of employment is governed by § 2 (2) Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz - WissZeitVG). A shorter contract term is possible by arrangement. Within the project Neuro-Symbolic AI with Logic-Memory Decomposition (Neuro-SAIL), a new class of architectures for verifiable neuro-symbolic AI is being researched using Logic-Memory Decomposition. Rule-based decisions are made by logic components, while memory modules are only used when information is incomplete or ambiguous. If no reliable decision is possible, escalation to humans occurs. The aim is to make rule-based decisions more transparent and efficient, to limit the use of neural models to necessary cases, and to reduce rule violations and unsubstantiated statements.Professional assignment: Chair of Scalable Software Architectures for Data Analytics (Prof. Dr. Michael Färber)Research areas: Natural Language Processing, Large Language Models, Knowledge Graphs, and related fields (e.g., Graph Machine Learning)Tasks: - scientific research and development activities in at least one of the above-mentioned research areas- participation in national and international research projects, possibly in collaboration with industry- preparation of publications in internationally renowned journals and presentation of research findings at conferencesRequirements: - a university degree (M.Sc., M.Eng. or equivalent) and if applicable a PhD degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Intelligent Systems, Data Science, Computational Science, Mathematics, Applied Statistics, Information Science, Information Systems, Information Systems Engineering, Electronic Information Engineering, Computational Linguistics, Digital Humanities, Linguistics, or a related field- a strong interest in fundamental research in the above-mentioned fields- strong programming skills, preferably in Python, including experience with deep learning frameworks (e.g. PyTorch, TensorFlow) and related tools- good written and spoken English- strong analytical and problem-solving skills- high level of motivation and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team- research experience (publications, theses, projects) in the above-mentioned research areas is a major advantageWe offer:The position comes with access to high-performance computing resources and access to training opportunities within ScaDS.AI.TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. We therefore expressly encourage women to apply. The university is a family-friendly university. We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities. If multiple candidates prove to be equally qualified, those with disabilities or with equivalent status pursuant to the German Social Code IX (SGB IX) will receive priority for employment.Application:Please submit your detailed application with the usual documents (e.g., cover letter, CV, and other supporting documents), quoting the job reference “ScaDS.AI Färber E 13” by November, 25, 2026 (stamped arrival date of the university central mail service or the time stamp on the email server of TUD applies), preferably via the TUD SecureMail Portal https://securemail.tu-dresden.de by sending it as a single pdf file to jobs-scads.ai@tu-dresden.de (https://mailto:jobs-scads.ai@tu-dresden.de) or to:TU Dresden, ScaDS.AI, Prof. Dr. Michael Färber, Helmholtzstr. 10, 01069 Dresden, Germany.Please submit copies only, as your application will not be returned to you. Expenses incurred in attending interviews cannot be reimbursed.TUD is a founding partner in the DRESDEN-concept alliance.Reference to data protection: Your data protection rights, the purpose for which your data will be processed, as well as further information about data protection is available to you on the website:https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis (https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis) .Ergänzende Informationen:Nur schwerbehinderte oder ihnen gleichgestellte PersonenAnforderungen an den Bewerber: Erweiterte Kenntnisse: Data Science, Forschung, Entwicklung, Informationswissenschaften, Mathematik, Informatik, Technische Informatik

jobs.occupation: Research associate (m/f/x) for the CRC 1844 "Episodic Memory", Subproject A16 (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.87 hours/week = 75%) 01.01.2027, pending funding approval, we are looking for oneResearch associate (m/f/x) for the CRC 1844 "Episodic Memory", Subproject A16The Department of Predictive Cognition is a newly established research unit within the Faculty of Psychology. After the completion of the new THINK research building on the former Opel site Mark 51°7, the team will move there https://www.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/think/index.html.en. The research focus of our department is on combining neuroimaging and behavioural measurements with computational models to understand how the human brain learns and uses prior expectations during cognition. More information can be found here: https://blanklab.eu/The position is part of the Collaborative Research Center “Episodic Memory” (CRC 1844), an interdisciplinary consortium consisting of researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy, and neuroscience. The basis for our research is the Scenario Construction Framework, which conceptualizes episodic memory as mental simulations of past episodes, constructed from episodic memory traces and semantic information. As a part of this team, you will be trained in interdisciplinary research and have access to a broad spectrum of initiatives to support you in your academic journey. When we communicate with others, our perception of their speech is continuously guided by the memory of our past interactions. But how? In this CRC subproject A16 " Integration of episodic traces and semantic other-person models in a social context", we will investigate how memory traces of previously heard dialogues and the other-person model, which contains general semantic knowledge about the person, modify speech perception. This project places the generative model of scenario construction within a social context. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging, we investigate how EM traces and other-person models differentially influence the neural representation of speech and language. We are looking for an enthusiastic researcher with a Master's degree in psychology, cognitive science, or a related field and strong programming and statistical skills to carry out the proposed project.Scope: part-timeDuration: fixed-term, 31.12.2030 (end of project)Start: 01.01.2027, pending funding approvalApply by:  2026-11-30Your tasks:- Organization and execution of experimental research work, from programming experimental setups, data acquisition, and data analysis, to the dissemination of the results- Acquisition of MRI data- Analysis and publication of MRI data- Practice of Open Science Practices- Close collaboration with PIs and ECRs from other subprojectsYour profile:- A Master of Science or an equivalent degree in neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology, or a related discipline- Strong programming and statistical skills- Experience in experimental approaches to study predictive processing, memory, learning, and communication- Prior experience with fMRI is an advantage- Experience and keen interest in using large language models- Strong organizational skills- A high level of spoken and written English- Highly self-motivated and eager to learn- Working independently, in a structured manner, and with a focus on results- Enjoy working as part of an interdisciplinary team of researchershttps://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/c0bf34da8b741897fe8de879edc88d7edfbdf8730?ref=AfA (https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/c0bf34da8b741897fe8de879edc88d7edfbdf8730?ref=AfA)

In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (19.915 hours/week = 50%) from 01.01.2027, pending funding approval, we are looking for anOutreach Coordinator (m,f,x)The Collaborative Research Center “Episodic Memory” (CRC 1844) is an interdisciplinary research consortium bringing together researchers from psychology, computational neuroscience, philosophy, and neuroscience. It comprises 18 subprojects led by 22 principal investigators across six universities and is coordinated at Ruhr University Bochum (RUB). CRC 1844 investigates episodic memory—the ability to remember specific events from one’s personal past—from multiple disciplinary perspectives. A central goal of the consortium is to communicate research on episodic memory and its relevance beyond the scientific community, foster dialogue between science and society, and to develop innovative educational and participatory formats for engaging different target groups with research on episodic memory.We are seeking an Outreach Coordinator to lead the strategic development, implementation, and coordination of outreach and science communication activities within CRC 1844. As the central point of contact for outreach, the coordinator will work closely with researchers across the consortium to communicate research on episodic memory to diverse audiences and foster dialogue between science and society. As a member of the coordination team they will develop and implementt public engagement and educational activities, support citizen science initiatives, coordinate the CRC’s digital presence, and collaborate with internal and external partners to strengthen the visibility and societal impact of the consortium’s research.Scope: part-timeDuration: fixed-term, 31.12.2030, pending funding approvalStart: from 01.01.2027, pending funding approvalApply by:  2026-11-29Your tasks:• Proactively engage with the CRC’s researchers to identify research findings, topics, and activities suitable for science communication and public engagement.• Develop accessible and engaging formats for communicating the CRC’s own research on episodic memory and that of others to different audiences, from children to older adults.• Develop, organize, and coordinate public engagement activities, including public lectures, workshops, exhibitions, discussion events, and activities for schools and other educational settings.• Co-design and implement target-group-specific curricula, educational formats, and materials across the CRC’s research areas in close collaboration with the Professional School of Education.• Support the development and implementation of citizen science initiatives associated with the CRC’s game and facilitate interaction between researchers and participating members of the public.• Build, maintain, and further develop the CRC’s digital presence, including its website and social media channels, and coordinate the creation and publication of digital content.• Produce and coordinate communication materials such as research stories, news items, newsletters, brochures, and other digital and print materials.• Support and advise researchers in communicating their work to non-specialist audiences and contribute to training in science communication and public engagement.• Establish and maintain relationships with university communication and outreach units, schools and other educational institutions, cultural organizations, and other relevant external partners.• Represent the CRC at public events, science festivals, exhibitions, and other outreach and science communication activities.• Monitor and evaluate the CRC’s outreach activities and use the results to continuously improve its outreach and communication strategy.Your profile:- A master’s degree, or equivalent, in educational science, science communication, media or digital studies, the humanities, psychology, cognitive science, or a closely related field- Excellent written and spoken The German Diabetes Center (DDZ), Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at the Heinrich Heine University (HHU) Düsseldorf is an interdisciplinary research institute that links basic and clinical sciences to improve prevention, diagnosis and therapy of Diabetes mellitus and its complications. We are seeking a talented and highly motivatedPostdoctoral Fellow (PhD/Dr. rer. nat., m/f/div., E13 TV-L 100%) to join our research group. WE ARE LOOKING FOR YOU ASPRODUCT SOFTWARE ENGINEER (BACK END JAVA) (M/W/D)LIMITED IN COLOGNEInterzero is one of the leading service providers in closing product, material, and logistics cycles and a pioneer in plastics recycling, operating Europe’s largest sorting capacity. Guided by the principle of “zero waste solutions,” the company supports more than 80,000 customers across Europe in the responsible handling of recyclable materials, helping them improve their sustainability performance and conserve primary  resources. With around 2,000 employees, Interzero generates annual revenues of nearly one billion euros. According to Fraunhofer UMSICHT, Interzero’s recycling activities alone saved approximately 1.04 million tons of greenhouse gas emissions and 8.09 million tons of primary raw  materials compared to primary production in 2024. Further information at: www.interzero.de.What is it about?- Collaboration: Together with Product, UX and Front-End colleagues, design and implement the Java back ends of both brand-new and evolving products you’ll stay with for the long haul.- Modeling: Translate business goals into sturdy domain models and reliable services that deliver real customer value.- Architecture: We’re moving toward a headless, microservice-oriented landscape. As a senior, you’ll help create clean APIs, refine coding standards and champion the right refactorings.- Automation: Build and refine GitLab pipelines, Docker images and workflow engines that remove manual steps - both in development and inside the products themselves.- Frontend partnership: Partner closely with front-end teams so the data, endpoints and performance they need are always there, making the user experience shine.- Leadership: Mentor junior engineers, run architecture sessions or even lead a small squad when it fits your personal goals.- Innovation: Experiment with new Java features, cloud services and patterns that help us close product loops faster. Your ideas are welcome.Advantages:- Job Security: You can expect a varied, exciting, and secure role with one of the largest environmental service providers in a future-proof industry.- Compensation: You receive performance-based pay with a strong focus on maintaining your work-life balance.- Flexibility: You benefit from flexible working hours and the option to work remotely.- Creative Freedom: You work in an environment where ideas, initiative, and creative freedom are encouraged and supported.- Flat Hierarchies: You operate within flat hierarchies and quickly take on responsibility for your own tasks.- Collaboration: You experience a culture of collaboration and respect at eye level, both within and beyond your team.- Development: You have access to internal and external training and development opportunities.- Health: You benefit from a comprehensive health management program.- Benefits: You receive attractive perks such as corporate benefits, bike leasing, free drinks and fruit on-site, and coverage of the Germany ticket or an Edenred card.Profile:- Experience: 5 + years of professional Java experience, ideally with Spring Boot and Hibernate/JPA.- Expertise: Deep knowledge of RESTful API design, relational databases (MySQL/PostgreSQL), and containerization with Docker.- Frontend-Familiarity: Familiarity with our frontend technology stack (React/Next.js/TypeScript) can be advantageous; if you want to work full-stack, you can.- DevOps: Familiarity with GitLab CI/CD — our DevOps team handles the heavy lifting, but you know your way around.- Architectural Judgment: A sense for clean architectures, test automation, and the judgement to choose the right pattern at the right time.- Languages: Fluent English (German is a bonus), a collaborative mindset and genuine curiosity about how products succeed in the real world.- EU-Work: A valid EU work permit; candidates already based in Germany (or nearby EU countries) are strongly preferred.Contact:Yannick Bartschhr@interzero.deErgänzende Informationen:Anforderungen an den Bewerber: Grundkenntnisse: Software testen, SoftwarearchitekturErweiterte Kenntnisse: Datenbankadministration, -management, -organisation, Backend-Entwicklung, Programmiersprache Java, REST (Representational State Transfer), Java Persistence API (JPA)

GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel is a foundation under public law jointly financed by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%) and the State of Schleswig-Holstein (10%). It is one of the internationally leading institutions in the field of marine research.Through our research and our commitment to the transfer of knowledge and technology, we contribute significantly to the preservation of the function and protection of the ocean for future generations.The Research Unit Magmatic and Hydrothermal Systems (MuHS) of the research division 4 - Dynamics of the Ocean Floor is offering a position preferably starting as soon as possible. The position offers the possibility to attain a doctoral degree in natural sciences.The position is within the framework of the project “Understanding Core-Mantle Interaction Through Global Mapping of Ultra-Low Velocity Zones in Mantle Convection Models”, which is part of the German Science Foundation's Priority Programm SPP 2404 DeepDyn (https://www.geo.lmu.de/deepdyn/en/) about reconstructing the deep dynamics of planet Earth over geologic time.Ultra-Low Velocity Zones (ULVZs) are thin patches at the base of Earth’s mantle-only tens of kilometres high yet 100 to 1000 km wide-where seismic shear waves exhibit extreme reductions of 20-30%. They are archives of Earth’s thermochemical evolution, potentially reflecting its early differentiation or interactions with the core, but also more recent mantle flow patterns. Yet these interpretations depend critically on ULVZ composition, which remains poorly constrained.The doctoral researcher will numerically model ULVZ evolution and properties in plate-guided global mantle convection simulations. They will develop a framework that quantitatively evaluates these simulations by inferring ULVZ properties from mineral physics and comparing them to seismic constraints, including ULVZ geometry, geographic location and distribution. They will synthesize these results to deliver the first global ULVZ map based on dynamic simulations and to discriminate among proposed ULVZ compositions. jobs.occupation: Doctoral researcher (m/f/d/x) in microbial systems biophysics (Biophysiker/in)
jobs.description: Founded in 1409, Leipzig University is one of Germany’s largest universities and a leader in research and medical training. With around 30,000 students and more than 5000 members of staff across 14 faculties, it is at the heart of the vibrant and outward-looking city of Leipzig. Leipzig University offers an innovative and international working environment as well as an exciting range of career opportunities in research, teaching, knowledge and technology transfer, infrastructure and administration.The Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics at the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics at the Faculty of Physics and Earth System Sciences, seeks to fill the above position.About the position- Salary group 13 TV-L - Fixed-term position in accordance with the training plan, initially for 1 year; an extension of the fixed-term contract is planned- 50 % of a full-time position- As soon as possibleThe newly formed Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics (https://home.uni-leipzig.de/sysbiophys/) , led by Professor Katja Taute, is part of the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics (https://www.physes.uni-leipzig.de/en/pdi) , which hosts a broad range of biophysics research. Active matter, including bacterial systems, is a growing key research area at the Institute. Our research group develops and uses biophysical methods, including high-throughput, 3D bacterial tracking and microfluidics, in combination with theory and simulations, to quantitatively analyse the spatio-temporal dynamics of bacteria at the level of individuals and populations. One research focus is the chemotactic navigation of bacteria in mechanically complex environments. In nature, swimming bacteria navigate relative to chemical stimuli in environments ranging from open waters to soil and the gut.The new doctoral researcher is to investigate how the gut bacterium E. coli navigates mechanically complex environments that mimic properties of its natural habitat. Properties of both the bacteria and the environment will be modulated in a controlled fashion to identify the underlying physical mechanisms and address the following questions:- What is the relationship between behavioural and material parameters that enable optimal navigation?- Is optimal intracellular information processing specific to the type of environment?- How do bacteria navigate mechanical gradients?The role- Independent, original, experimental scientific research on the above project- Additional scientific qualification (preparing a doctoral thesis)- Thorough documentation of research- Publication of research results, for example at conferences, workshops, or in scientific articles- Contributions to the Institute’s teaching responsibilitiesAbout you- An excellent scientific university degree (master of science or comparable) in (bio-)physics, (bio-)engineering or a related field- Very good command of at least one programming language (Matlab or Python preferred) and of quantitative scientific data analysis- A track record of academic excellence (e.g. very good grades in the course of study, research or study scholarships and prizes, scientific publications)- Written and spoken professional fluency in English (at least equivalent to level B2)- Excellent written communication skills, demonstrated through coherent, structured and precise writing- Experience with microscopy and scientific image processing would be an advantage- Interest in quantitative experimental interdisciplinary science- Collaborative mindset and teamwork skillsWhat we offer you- a varied role with a high degree of responsibility in the dynamic environment of a major university- a professional English-language work environment at the leading edge of interdisciplinary science- Collaboration in a friendly, supportive and motivated team- flexible working hours and mobile working to support work-life balance- Goal-oriented staff development throughout your working life, with opportunities for continuing professional development- a wide range of occupational health management services - Remuneration in line with the collective bargaining agreement of the federal states (TV-L), including an annual special payment and occupational pension scheme- excellent transport links and the option to purchase a discounted public transport ticket, such as the Deutschlandticket as a commuter pass- a wide range of food options in the refectories and cafés operated by Studentenwerk Leipzig.Leipzig University aims to increase the proportion of women in positions of responsibility and therefore expressly invites qualified women to apply. Severely disabled persons – or persons deemed legally equal to them under Book IX of the German Social Code – are encouraged to apply and will be given preference in the case of equal suitability. If you have any questions about accessibility or need assistance with this application process, please contact Leipzig University’s disability officers at: schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de (https://mailto:schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de) .Have we sparked your interest?Please submit your application in English addressed to Fakultät für Physik und Erdsystemwissenschaften, Herrn Dekan Professor Dr. Johannes Quaas by 15 November 2026 (Extension of the Deadline) via our online application portal.Please include the following documents with your application:- A short letter of motivation (max. 1 page) in which you clearly explain why you would like to work on this project- A scientific CV (evidence of creative and independent scientific work is an advantage)- The names and contact information of two people who have agreed to provide academic references- Academic transcripts clearly listing the courses taken and grades achieved in your entire scientific higher education (bachelor’s as well as master’s or comparable degrees)

jobs.occupation: Post-Doc position: AI-Driven Robotic Experimentation for Controlling Metal Degradation (Chemiker/in)
jobs.description: Metal degradation can be a boon or a bane, depending on the application and on how well we can control it. A corroding car component is a safety risk. A biodegradable metal implant that dissolves at exactly the right rate spares patients a second surgery. An aqueous battery lives or dies depending on what happens at its electrodes.At the Department of Electrochemistry and Big Data we unravel degradation pathways of light metals used in structural applications, medical devices and aqueous batteries. For these applications, degradation can be controlled using tailored electrolyte additives. The chemical space of possible additives is virtually infinite, so we do not test one-by-one. We run a robotic, high-throughput testing platform coupled with machine learning and AI agents that help to decide which experiment to run next. Join us to build the self-driving laboratory of corrosion science.We are offering a 2‑year Post-Doctoral position, as soon as possible, in the quickly developing field of robotic experimentation in materials science. The position is full-time (39 h/week) and will be located in Hereon's main campus, in Geesthacht (near Hamburg).We value diversity and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. We particularly encourage qualified women to apply.Your tasks- Run and extend automated experimental workflows on our robotic platform to test how light alloys respond to electrolytes of increasing complexity- Discover high-performing organic and inorganic compounds that control degradation for structural and biomedical applications- Work side by side with computational scientists to build structure-property models, and use AI agents to accelerate screening- Uncover the mechanisms behind effective degradation control, and turn them into design rules for pre-selecting promising compounds- Publish your results in leading journals, present at international conferences, write project reports and contribute to open, FAIR datasetsYour profile- A completed master's and PhD degree in chemistry, electrochemistry, materials science, computational materials science or a related field- Solid experimental skills in chemical laboratories and confidence in quantitative data analysis using appropriate software- Experience with corrosion, electrochemical methods or light alloys (Mg, Al, Zn)- Experience with lab automation, electronic lab notebooks, FAIR data, databases or machine learning- Curiosity about automation and AI, and motivation to work at the interface of experiment and computation- Very good English, knowledge of the German language is preferred but not mandatory, we support language learningContent-related enquiries regarding this position can be directed to Sviatlana.Lamaka(at)hereon.de.Our offer- Access to state-of-the-art (robotic) labs, unique scientific and technical infrastructure- Access to a large international research and industrial network.- Funding for conferences, summer schools and courses needed or research stays- An exciting and varied job in a research center with around 1,000 employees from more than 60 nations- An International Welcome Office with guest accommodation- 6 weeks holiday per year; company holidays between Christmas and New Year's DaySocial benefits under the collective agreement for the German public sector and remuneration up to pay grade 13 (EntgO Bund)A well-connected research campus, good networking opportunities, a subsidized Deutschlandticket (job ticket) subject to certain conditions, and charging facilities for electric vehicles- Individual opportunities for further training- An excellent technical infrastructure and modern workplace equipment- A family-friendly working environment with childcare options, e. g. a daycare center close to the workplace- Workplace health promotion programmes, e.g. an Employee Assistance Program (EAP)- Corporate Benefits- A varied canteen offering on campusSchwerbehinderte und diesen gleichgestellte behinderte Personen werden bei gleicher Qualifikation und Eignung im Rahmen der gesetzlichen Bestimmungen bevorzugt berücksichtigt.Bitte bewerben Sie sich mit Ihrem vollständigen Bewerbungsprofil (Lebenslauf, Motivationsschreiben, sonstige Referenzen) über unsere Karriereseite.

jobs.description: Du (w/m/d) bist Logopäde, Atem-, Sprech- und Stimmlehrer, Sprachtherapeut, o. Ä. oder kurz davor deinen Abschluss zu machen?- Du arbeitest zuverlässig und motiviert?- Du willst eigene Ideen verwirklichen?- Du möchtest eigenständig und selbstverantwortlich arbeiten?- Du möchtest dir deine Arbeitszeiten selbst flexibel einteilen?- Du bist interessiert daran als Teammitglied eine wachsende und junge Praxis zu bereichern?Dann bist Du bei uns genau richtig.Was dich erwartetAnfang 2021 eröffneten wir die Praxis in Herne-Wanne und suchen jetzt Verstärkung in Vollzeit. Gerne auch in Teilzeit oder auf 556-€-Basis! Im Team sind sowohl Berufseinsteiger/-innen als auch erfahrene Therapeut/-innen oder Wiedereinsteiger/-innen willkommen.Bei uns werden alle sprach-, sprech-, stimm- und schlucktherapeutischen Störungsbilder in jeder Altersklasse diagnostiziert, therapiert und sowohl ambulant als auch im Hausbesuch oder in kooperierenden Einrichtungen behandelt. Unsere Arbeit ist ganzheitlich und ressourcenorientiert. Die Praxis bietet nicht nur Therapien sondern auch IGeL-Leistungen bestimmter Behandlungsgebiete an. Der regelmäßige Austausch und die Klärung offener Fragen und Wünsche sorgt für ein gutes Betriebsklima und während der Einarbeitungszeit steht dir Inhaberin Katharina Schneider (https://katharina-schneider.net/ueber-uns/#katharina-schneider)  besonders intensiv zur Seite.Die Praxis bietet große, helle und freundliche Räumlichkeiten und ist über eine mobile Rampe barrierefrei zugänglich. Sie verfügt über drei gut ausgestattete Therapieräume, einen kleinen Wartebereich, ein rollstuhlgerechtes WC für die Patient/-innen sowie eine Küche und ein getrenntes Mitarbeiter WC. Sollten dir Spiele, Diagnostik- und Therapiematerial für deine Arbeit fehlen, schaffen wir diese an. Parkplätze und öffentliche Verkehrsmittel sind fußläufig schnell zu erreichen.In der Praxis wird tiergestützt gearbeitet. Ida (https://katharina-schneider.net/ueber-uns/#ida) , eine Border Collie Hündin, arbeitet in der Praxis mit den Patienten als Co-Therapeutin.Deine AufgabenDeine Aufgaben umfassen die Diagnostik, Förderung und Behandlung aller Störungsbilder in der Praxis, mit der Möglichkeit einer Spezialisierung auf bestimmte Behandlungsgebiete.Wir bieten:- eine faire Bezahlung mit Festgehalt ohne Minusstunden- bezahlte Vor- und Nachbereitungszeit- einen unbefristeten Arbeitsvertrag- eine Stelle, die flexibel nach deinen Bedürfnissen gestaltet wird, um eine ausgewogene Work-Life-Balance zu gewährleisten- regelmäßige Fortbildungen (inkl. Fortbildungsurlaub)- Patientenverwaltung und Terminplanung über eine Praxissoftware- einen sicheren Arbeitsplatz- ein eigenes Diensthandy mit VertragBeginn: sofort oder späterBerufserfahrung: egalFührerschein: Klasse B (wünschenswert)Wir erarbeiten gerne mit dir gemeinsam was dir wichtig ist und basteln dann dein „Paket“!Klingt gut? Dann melde dich ganz unkompliziert per Mail oder ruf uns einfach an und wir lernen uns bei einem Gespräch kennen.Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung!Are you (f/m/d) a speech therapist, respiratory therapist, speech and voice coach, or speech therapist, or similar, or are you about to graduate?Are you reliable and motivated?Do you want to realize your own ideas?Do you want to work independently and responsibly?Do you want to organize your working hours flexibly?Are you interested in enriching a growing and young practice as a team member?Then you've come to the right place.What awaits youWe opened our practice in Herne-Wanne at the beginning of 2021 and are now looking for full-time support. Part-time positions or a €556 salary are also welcome! Our team welcomes both newcomers to the profession and experienced therapists, as well as those returning to work.We diagnose and treat all speech, language, voice, and swallowing disorders for all age groups, both on an outpatient basis and through home visits or in partner facilities. Our work is holistic and resource-oriented. The practice offers not only therapies but also IGeL services for specific treatment areas. Regular communication and clarification of any open questions and requests ensures a positive working atmosphere, and owner Katharina Schneider will be there to support you intensively during your induction period.The practice offers large, bright, and welcoming spaces and is wheelchair accessible via a mobile ramp. It has three well-equipped therapy rooms, a small waiting area, a wheelchair-accessible restroom for patients, a kitchen, and a separate staff restroom. If you need games, diagnostic, and therapy materials for your work, we can provide them. Parking and public transportation are within easy walking distance.The practice uses animal-assisted therapy. Ida, a Border Collie, works alongside patients as a co-therapist.Your tasksYour tasks will include the diagnosis, support, and treatment of all disorders in the practice, with the possibility of specializing in specific treatment areas.We offer:- Fair compensation with a fixed salary without negative hours- Paid preparation and follow-up time- A permanent employment contract- A position that can be flexibly tailored to your needs to ensure a healthy work-life balance- Regular training (including training leave)- Patient management and appointment scheduling via practice software- A secure job- A company cell phone with a contractStart: immediately or laterProfessional experience: irrelevantDriver's license: Class B (desirable)We would be happy to work with you to determine what's important to you and then put together your "package"!Sounds good? Then simply contact us by email or give us a call and we'll get to know each other during a chat.We look forward to receiving your application!Information for applicants from abroad:We also welcome applicants from abroad.We support you in your search for an apartment.We expect German knowledge at a level from B1.Für Bewerber/Bewerberinnen, die Ihren festen Wohnsitz im Ausland haben: Die Zentrale Auslands- und Fachvermittlung (ZAV) hilft Ihnen bei der Arbeitssuche in Deutschland. jobs.occupation: (Senior) Legal Counsel, Sustainable Aviation Fuel & Energy Regulation (m/f/d) (Fachanwalt/-anwältin)
jobs.description: DHL Group is the world’s leading logistics provider. We connect people and markets and enable global trade. Our ambition is to be the first choice for customers, employees and investors worldwide. Sustainable aviation is transforming rapidly, and regulation is evolving with it. At DHL Group, you will work at the intersection of law, sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), international regulation and commercial business.In this (senior) legal role, you will advise our businesses on complex regulatory and contractual questions surrounding sustainable aviation fuels and aviation fuel regulation. Your work will cover emerging frameworks such as ReFuelEU Aviation, RED III and ICAO CORSIA, as well as innovative concepts such as Book & Claim. (Senior) Legal Counsel, Sustainable Aviation Fuel & Energy Regulation (m/f/d) Bonn | full-time | permanent Your Responsibilities* Act as a (senior) legal advisor on Sustainable Aviation Fuel, aviation fuel regulation and related ESG matters, supporting DHL Group businesses in an international environment.* Monitor and assess regulatory developments, particularly ReFuelEU Aviation, RED III and ICAO CORSIA, and translate their implications into actionable recommendations for the business.* Advise on Book & Claim structures, including certification requirements, chains of custody and recognition across different jurisdictions.* Draft, review and negotiate complex commercial contracts, including supplier framework agreements, SAF supply arrangements and Book & Claim agreements.* Develop legally robust approaches to SAF-related fuel investments, supply frameworks and commercial solutions.* Partner with Procurement, Finance and other specialist functions to develop implementation strategies that meet regulatory and commercial requirements.* Provide legal support on sustainability-related aspects of investments, M&A transactions, partnerships and joint ventures.* Represent DHL Group in relevant industry forums and networks and share regulatory knowledge through training and guidance for internal stakeholders Your profile* A degree in law or a comparable legal qualification. International legal qualifications are explicitly welcome.* Several years of relevant legal advisory experience, ideally gained within an international corporate environment.* Strong knowledge of ESG, energy, fuels and/or related regulatory matters. Experience in aviation or energy is an advantage.* Extensive experience drafting, reviewing and negotiating sophisticated commercial agreements.* The ability to analyse regulatory change and translate it into practical recommendations and implementation approaches.* Fluent written and spoken English, including the ability to negotiate effectively. German and additional languages are advantageous.* Strong analytical, communication, negotiation and stakeholder-management capabilities and the confidence to work independently in a rapidly evolving international regulatory environment.       Why Join This Role? This is an opportunity to take ownership of legal topics that sit directly at the intersection of aviation, sustainability, regulation and international commerce.Rather than advising from the sidelines, you will work closely with the business to help turn evolving regulatory requirements into commercial solutions and contribute to DHL Group's wider decarbonization ambitions Your Benefits* Flexibility: Work remotely for up to three days per week, combined with flexible working hours and no core working hours. Arrangements may vary depending on the role and responsibilities.* Workplace & Campus: Work at the Post Campus in Bonn alongside colleagues from more than 60 countries, with excellent transport connections, parking, cafés, restaurants and additional on-site services.* Learning & Development: Benefit from structured onboarding, on-the-job-training, networking, coaching and extensive professional development opportunities.* More for you: Benefits include our employee share programme, company pension plan, mobility offerings, employee discounts, family support, health and inclusion services, sabbatical opportunities and more. Ready to make an impact?* If you are an experienced legal professional who enjoys combining regulatory expertise with commercial problem-solving, we would like to hear from you.* Apply now using the application button with your complete application and salary expectations.* For an initial conversation or questions about the position, please contact Sven Rötzel (DHL Group, HR) at sven.roetzel@dhl.com or +49 228 189 52128.     “We are committed to equal opportunity and reject any forms of discrimination as defined in DHL Group’s Human Rights Policy Statement. The basis for employee selection at DHL Group is qualification, performance, skills and experience.”
